availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

# BusLink Studio: epics and sprint plan (BMAD phase 3–4)

Each epic becomes one Kiro feature spec in `.kiro/specs/<epic>/` and is executed by the `buslink-builder` agent. `ics-security-reviewer` reviews every epic commit, and the builder fixes its findings.

| # | Epic (Kiro spec) | PRD | Done when | Target (WIB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | `core-protocol`: RTU/TCP framing, CRC, codec, profile schema, quality model, scheduler, fake transport, property tests | R4–R9, R7 | `cargo test` green; PBT for CRC/framing/codec/order; dead-device fairness test | Nov 13 |
| E2 | `simulator`: in-process soil/VFD/temp/energy devices, fault injection, loopback RTU + TCP server | R10, R24 | Sim drives all E1 tests; VFD/temp state machines respond to writes | Nov 14 |
| E3 | `app-shell-desktop`: Tauri 2 app, Windows serial transport (VID:PID detect), sample bus, historian, CSV/XLSX/JSON export | R1, R3, R12, R20, R21 | Windows exe reads the simulator + the real BGT-SMPS on the CH343G; export opens in Excel | Nov 17 |
| E4 | `dashboard-ui`: connection center, ISA-101 live tiles, uPlot gap-aware trends, register inspector, alarms, i18n id/en, training mode | R12–R16, R24, N3, N4 | Headless Chrome journey 1 passes; WCAG checks; 360 px layout | Nov 21 |
| E5 | `commissioning-control`: command service state machine, ID/baud wizard, simulated VFD/temperature control panel, audit, reports | R17–R19, N1 | Journey 4 passes; the guard hook blocks writes outside `command/` | Nov 24 |
| E6 | `android-otg`: Kotlin USB plugin (usb-serial-for-android), permission, FGS, SAF export, APK | R2 | APK reads the real sensor on the A35 via OTG (journey 2) | Nov 26 |
| E7 | `lan-mqtt`: axum read-only LAN dashboard (token + TLS), MQTT 5 telemetry with outbox | R22, R23 | Journeys 3 and 5 pass | Nov 28 |
| E8 | `release`: NSIS + portable exe, APK, README/judge guide, evidence matrix, Remotion video, SolidCraft 3D, submission kit | N5, N6 | Release published; video < 3 min; Devpost submitted | Dec 2 |

content.text:

# Kiro ↔ omp handoff

Kiro builds BusLink Studio: specs, custom agents, hooks and steering in `.kiro/`, plus the code changes. omp (or any other terminal agent) only orchestrates. It starts Kiro sessions through the bridge, then reviews and verifies what Kiro produced. That split keeps the competition requirement honest: the work submitted is work Kiro did, and every session leaves evidence.

## How to run a Kiro task

```sh
# from the repository root (WSL or Linux shell)
python3 tools/kiro_bridge.py --agent ghostwire-builder --label "phantom-writer task 2" \
  "Execute task 2 of .kiro/specs/ot-security-lab/tasks.md"
```

- The bridge runs `kiro-cli chat --v3 --no-interactive --output-format stream-json`. It streams Kiro's answer and appends an entry to `docs/kiro-log/LEDGER.md` (agent, session ID, tools, changed files, credits). The raw transcript goes to `docs/kiro-log/runs/`.
- To continue a session, pass `--resume-id <session>` with the session ID from the ledger.
- Interactive work in the Kiro IDE or `kiro-cli` is equally valid. Add a short ledger entry by hand afterwards.

## Rules for the orchestrator

1. Do not edit product code or `.kiro/` directly. Ask Kiro to make the change. Direct edits are limited to `tools/`, `docs/kiro-log/` and release packaging, and each one must be listed in `docs/existing-code-disclosure.md`.
2. Review Kiro's diff and run the checks (`tools/dotnet run --project csharp/BusLink Studio.Tests/BusLink Studio.Tests.csproj`). If something fails, send the failure back to Kiro rather than patching it yourself.
3. Do not invent Kiro usage. `docs/kiro-usage.md` cites only ledger entries.
4. Commit after each verified Kiro task, with a message like `feat(kiro): <task> [session <id>]`.

## Environment

- Kiro CLI 3.2.0 or later, logged in (`kiro-cli whoami`).
- The .NET 8 SDK. The repository lives on `/mnt/d`, so `tools/dotnet` forwards to Windows `dotnet.exe`.

content.text:
Output:
  - Simulated VFD (`simulated`).
  - Simulated temperature controller (`simulated`).
  - Simulated energy meter (`simulated`).
  - A generic holding-register template.
- **R11 Import:** CSV/XLSX register map with preview and address-base detection. `.mbmap` read-only import (P2).

### UI
- **R12 Connection center:** ports/adapters, USB permission state, serial settings, TCP host, link statistics (TX/RX, CRC, timeouts, cycle time).
- **R13 Live dashboard:** ISA-101 high-performance style (grey base, color only for abnormal states, analog bar with normal range). Tiles show value, unit, quality text and age. Density toggle; Indonesian and English.
- **R14 Trends:** multiple tags with unit axes, cursor, zoom. **Gaps for lost communication, never interpolated.** Raw samples separate from display decimation (min-max). Alarm bands.
- **R15 Register inspector:** doc address, PDU offset, raw hex, decoded value in all four orders side by side, and the last request/response frame.
- **R16 Alarms (ISA-18.2):** threshold, hysteresis/deadband, on/off delay, priority, acknowledge, shelve with expiry. Communication alarms kept separate from process alarms. Alarm log.
- **R17 Commissioning wizard:** change unit ID or baud on one device, with journal → write → reconnect at the new settings → read-back → pass/fail. A recovery hint shows the old settings.
- **R18 Control panel (simulated VFD + temperature controller):**
  - The command service requires the device to be armed (session timeout), checks bounds, and asks for confirmation with an explicit label ("Apply setpoint 40.0 °C").
  - It encodes a frame preview, writes once (no automatic retry), reads back, and records the audit entry.
  - A software stop is always reachable and labeled "not an E-stop".
- **R19 Reports:** session summary (devices, profile versions, quality statistics, alarms, commands) exported as PDF/HTML.

### Data
- **R20 Historian:** SQLite WAL with tables sessions, devices, tags, samples, events, commands, outbox. Logging interval separate from polling interval. Retention setting.
- **R21 Export:** CSV (UTF-8, ISO-8601 UTC, quality and age columns, formula-injection guard), XLSX (Measurements, Devices, Configuration, Events, Commands sheets, numbers kept as numbers), JSON. Android saves through SAF.

### Sharing
- **R22 LAN dashboard:** opt-in. The app serves the same frontend (read-only routes + WebSocket stream) on a user-chosen interface/port, with a per-session token, TLS (self-signed per session; the URL/QR carries the token), and no write endpoints. Works from Windows and Android.
- **R23 MQTT telemetry:** opt-in. MQTT 5 over TLS, topic `buslink/{site}/{gateway}/{device}/{tag}` or a Sparkplug-B-compatible namespace (decision in architecture), payload with ts/seq/value/unit/quality/profile_version, a bounded offline outbox, deduplication by sequence. Credentials go in the OS secret store and never into project files.

### Training
- **R24 Simulator:** built-in multi-device RTU-over-loopback and TCP simulator with the bundled simulated profiles. Fault injection: timeout, CRC error, exception, stale, wrong word order. A **training mode** with guided exercises in Indonesian and English.

## 4. Non-functional requirements
- **N1 Safety:** read-only by default. Writes only through the command service. No broadcast writes. Audit trail for every command.

content.text:
Output:
## 2. Alarm management: ANSI/ISA-18.2-2016 / IEC 62682:2022 / EEMUA 191 (4th ed.)

**Alarm states.** The ISA-18.2 state model, as summarised by ICONICS and the IEC 62682 preview:
- Normal
- **Unacknowledged** (active, not acked)
- **Acknowledged** (active, acked)
- **Return-to-normal unacknowledged** (cleared but not acked)
- **Shelved** (manually suppressed by the operator, with an expiry)
- **Suppressed by design** (by logic or state)
- **Out of service** (maintenance)

Latching alarms stay active until acknowledged.

**Performance targets.** Figures are from ISA and EEMUA summaries (ISA ie KPI paper, ProcessVue, Siemens white paper):
- Average alarm rate per operator: about 1 per 10 minutes is "very likely acceptable"; about 2 per 10 minutes is "maximum manageable".
- **Flood:** more than 10 alarms per 10 minutes.
- Priority distribution: about **80 % low / 15 % medium / 5 % high**.
- Standing alarms: under 5. Chattering alarms (≥ 3 in 1 minute) are a defect to fix.

**Deadband and delay starting points** (ISA-18.2 practice tables, cited in vendor guides):

| Process variable | Deadband | On/off delay |
|---|---|---|
| Flow, level | 5 % of range | 15 s |
| Pressure | 2 % | 15 s |
| Temperature | 1 % | 60 s |

**BusLink rules**
- **Alarm definition:** tag, type (HI/HIHI/LO/LOLO/ROC/quality), limit, deadband, on-delay, off-delay, priority (1–3), message, latch flag.
- **Engine:** implements the seven states above, including shelve-with-expiry and out-of-service. Alarms stay active while acknowledged.
- **Communication alarms** (timeout, CRC, disconnected) are a separate class from **process alarms**, so a dead link does not raise a flood of process alarms.
- **Alarm banner:**
  - Shows the count per priority and the oldest unacknowledged alarm.
  - The alarm list is sortable and filterable.
  - Acknowledge and shelve are logged events.
- A **flood indicator** appears when more than 10 alarms occur in 10 minutes. A chattering detector flags any alarm that fires 3 or more times in 1 minute.
- Default deadbands follow the table above, by unit type in the profile.

---

## 5. Security: IEC 62443 and Modbus/TCP Security

- **IEC 62443 security levels:**
  - SL1: casual or coincidental violation.
  - SL2: intentional, simple means.
  - SL3: sophisticated means.
  - SL4: extended resources.
- **Foundational requirements:**
  - FR1: identification and authentication.
  - FR2: use control.
  - FR3: system integrity.
  - FR4: data confidentiality.
  - FR5: restricted data flow.
  - FR6: timely response to events.
  - FR7: resource availability.
- **Relevant 62443-4-2 component requirements:**
  - CR 1.1: human user identification and authentication.
  - CR 2.1: authorization=<redacted>  - CR 2.8: auditable events.
  - CR 3.1: communication integrity.
  - CR 4.1: information confidentiality.
- **Zones and conduits:** the tool sits on the engineering side, and the RS485 bus is its own zone.
- **Modbus/TCP Security** (Modbus.org): TLS 1.2+ on **port 802**, mutual X.509 authentication, and an X.509 v3 **role extension** carrying a role used for authorization. Legacy Modbus TCP (port 502) has no authentication.

**BusLink rules**
- **Read-only by default (FR2).** Writes need explicit arming per device, with a session timeout, and go through the command service only.
- An audit record for every arm, write, read-back, acknowledge and shelve (CR 2.8). Each record carries the user/session, device, profile version, and request/response hex.
- **LAN dashboard (FR4/FR5):**
  - Off by default; binds to one chosen interface.
  - Uses TLS (self-signed per session) plus a random token.
  - Read-only routes, no write endpoints; rate-limited.
- **Secrets** (MQTT passwords) go in the OS keychain or Android Keystore. They never appear in profiles, projects, exports or logs.
- **Profiles are data only.** They are validated against a JSON Schema, and expressions are limited to scale/offset; no scripts.
- Modbus/TCP Security (port 802) is a later transport option and is out of scope for the MVP. The docs must say so clearly.

---

## 2. Alarm management: ANSI/ISA-18.2-2016 / IEC 62682:2022 / EEMUA 191 (4th ed.)

**Alarm states.** The ISA-18.2 state model, as summarised by ICONICS and the IEC 62682 preview:
- Normal
- **Unacknowledged** (active, not acked)
- **Acknowledged** (active, acked)
- **Return-to-normal unacknowledged** (cleared but not acked)
- **Shelved** (manually suppressed by the operator, with an expiry)
- **Suppressed by design** (by logic or state)
- **Out of service** (maintenance)

Latching alarms stay active until acknowledged.

**Performance targets.** Figures are from ISA and EEMUA summaries (ISA ie KPI paper, ProcessVue, Siemens white paper):
- Average alarm rate per operator: about 1 per 10 minutes is "very likely acceptable"; about 2 per 10 minutes is "maximum manageable".
- **Flood:** more than 10 alarms per 10 minutes.
- Priority distribution: about **80 % low / 15 % medium / 5 % high**.
- Standing alarms: under 5. Chattering alarms (≥ 3 in 1 minute) are a defect to fix.

**Deadband and delay starting points** (ISA-18.2 practice tables, cited in vendor guides):

| Process variable | Deadband | On/off delay |
|---|---|---|
| Flow, level | 5 % of range | 15 s |
| Pressure | 2 % | 15 s |
| Temperature | 1 % | 60 s |

**BusLink rules**
- **Alarm definition:** tag, type (HI/HIHI/LO/LOLO/ROC/quality), limit, deadband, on-delay, off-delay, priority (1–3), message, latch flag.
- **Engine:** implements the seven states above, including shelve-with-expiry and out-of-service. Alarms stay active while acknowledged.
- **Communication alarms** (timeout, CRC, disconnected) are a separate class from **process alarms**, so a dead link does not raise a flood of process alarms.
- **Alarm banner:**
  - Shows the count per priority and the oldest unacknowledged alarm.
  - The alarm list is sortable and filterable.
  - Acknowledge and shelve are logged events.
- A **flood indicator** appears when more than 10 alarms occur in 10 minutes. A chattering detector flags any alarm that fires 3 or more times in 1 minute.
- Default deadbands follow the table above, by unit type in the profile.

---

  - SL1: casual or coincidental violation.

- **Foundational requirements:**
  - FR1: identification and authentication.
  - FR2: use control.

You are the BusLink Studio builder. You implement exactly one spec task per run from `.kiro/specs/*/tasks.md`, then stop and report.

Before coding:

While coding:
- Follow `tech.md` for layout and commands, `modbus.md` for protocol rules, `ui.md` for the UI, `android.md` for Android.

                expected: "confirmed",
                actual: self.state(),
            });

        self.ensure_armed()?;
        let Inner::Confirmed(plan) = std::mem::replace(&mut self.inner, Inner::Sent) else {
            return Err(CommandError::WrongState {
                expected: "confirmed",
                actual: self.state(),
            });
        };
        let Plan {
            preview,
            frame,
            readback_request,
            readback_type,
            readback_register,
            compare,
        } = *plan;
        let mut sent_rec = self.plan_record(AuditEvent::Sent, &preview);
        sent_rec.note = Some("about to send (single attempt)".into());
        // Fail closed: no audit record, no write.
        if let Err(e) = self.audit.append(&sent_rec) {
            let outcome = CommandOutcome {
                preview_id: preview.id,
                ack: Ack::Invalid("not sent: audit log unavailable".into()),
                readback: Readback::Unknown,
                readback_value: None,
                readback_raw: None,
                readback_error: None,
                request_hex: preview.frame_hex.clone(),
                response_hex: String::new(),
                audit_error: Some(e.to_string()),
            };
            self.inner = Inner::Failed(Box::new(outcome));
            return Err(e.into());
        }

        let request = frame.request.clone();
        let unit = frame.unit;
        let record = link.send(frame);
        if !record.request.is_empty() {
            self.sends += 1;
        }
        let ack = match &record.outcome {
            Ok(reply) => match request.verify_echo(reply) {
                Ok(()) => Ack::Acknowledged,
                Err(_) => Ack::BadEcho,
            },
            Err(ExchangeError::Exception(c)) => Ack::Exception(c.0),
            Err(ExchangeError::Timeout) => Ack::Timeout,
            Err(ExchangeError::Crc(_)) => Ack::CrcError,
            Err(ExchangeError::Link(_)) if record.request.is_empty() => Ack::NotSent,
            Err(ExchangeError::Link(_)) => Ack::LinkLost,
            Err(e @ (ExchangeError::Decode(_) | ExchangeError::Encode(_))) => Ack::Invalid(e.to_string()),
        };

        self.inner = Inner::ReadBack;
        let (readback, readback_value, readback_raw, readback_error) = if matches!(ack, Ack::LinkLost | Ack::NotSent) {
            (Readback::Unknown, None, None, Some("link lost".to_owned()))
        } else {
            match link.read(unit, readback_request) {
                Err(e) => (Readback::Unknown, None, None, Some(e.to_string())),
                Ok(data) => {
                    let words = data.as_words();
                    let decoded = codec::decode(readback_type, readback_register.word_order, &words)
                        .and_then(|r| codec::to_engineering(&r, &readback_register.scaling().without_range()));
                    let value = decoded.as_ref().ok().copied().flatten();
                    let verdict = match &compare {
                        Compare::SameRaw(expected) => {
                            if *expected == words {
                                Readback::Verified
                            } else {
                                Readback::Mismatch
                            }
                        }
                        Compare::Expected(e, tol) => match value {
                            Some(v) if (v - e).abs() <= *tol => Readback::Verified,
                            Some(_) => Readback::Mismatch,
                            None => Readback::Unknown,
                        },
                        Compare::Report => Readback::Unknown,
                    };
                    (verdict, value, Some(words), decoded.err().map(|e| e.to_string()))
                }
            }
        };

        let mut outcome = CommandOutcome {
            preview_id: preview.id,
            ack: ack.clone(),
            readback,
            readback_value,
            readback_raw,
            readback_error,
            request_hex: hex_spaced(&record.request),
            response_hex: hex_spaced(&record.response),
            audit_error: None,
        };
        let mut rec = sent_rec;
        rec.event = Some(AuditEvent::Result);
        rec.ts_ms = self.clock.utc_ms();
        rec.request_hex = Some(outcome.request_hex.clone());
        rec.response_hex = Some(outcome.response_hex.clone());
        rec.exception = match ack {
            Ack::Exception(c) => Some(c),
            _ => None,
        };
        rec.ack = Some(ack.as_str());
        rec.readback = Some(readback.as_str().into());
        rec.readback_value = readback_value;
        rec.note = outcome.readback_error.clone();
        if let Err(e) = self.audit.append(&rec) {
            outcome.audit_error = Some(e.to_string());
        }
        let link_lost = matches!(ack, Ack::LinkLost | Ack::NotSent);
        self.inner = if ack == Ack::Acknowledged {
            Inner::Done(Box::new(outcome.clone()))
        } else {
            Inner::Failed(Box::new(outcome.clone()))
        };
        if link_lost {
            // Arming is dropped on link loss; the outcome stays visible.
            let mut r = self.base_record(AuditEvent::Disarm);
            r.note = Some(DisarmReason::LinkLost.as_str().into());
            let _ = self.audit.append(&r);
            self.armed = None;
        } else {
            self.refresh();
        }
        Ok(outcome)
    }
}

//! Session service (app-shell-desktop design §2): links, one worker per link,
//! devices, the hub that feeds the live store, alarms and historian, plus
//! trend, export and inspector queries. Platform code supplies transports
//! through a factory, so this module never links serial drivers, Tauri or
//! the simulator.
//!
//! There is no write path here: monitoring only (safety rules 1–2). Control
//! goes through `crate::command` (epic E5).
//!
//! Lock order: `links` → `live` → `alarms` → `log` → `historian`.

pub mod frames;
pub mod live;

use crate::alarm::{AlarmDef, AlarmEngine, AlarmError, AlarmEvent, AlarmSnapshot};
use crate::bus::{BusRecv, SampleBus};
use crate::clock::Clock;
use crate::codec::{self, TypeName};
use crate::device::{DeviceError, DeviceInstance, LinkConfig, LinkKind};
use crate::export::{self, ExportDoc};
use crate::historian::batch::{LogDecimator, SampleBatcher};
use crate::historian::{DeviceRow, EventRow, Historian, SessionInfo};
use crate::poll::scheduler::{DeviceCounters, FrameTap, LinkScheduler, SchedulerError};
use crate::poll::worker::{LinkState as WorkerState, LinkWorker, SampleSink};
use crate::profile::{Profile, Text};
use crate::protocol::pdu::ExceptionCode;
use crate::quality::{Quality, Sample};
use crate::transport::{LinkRegistry, Transport, TransportError};
use crate::trend::{self, TrendInput, TrendSeries};
use frames::{FrameEntry, FrameLog};
use live::{LiveStore, TagView, TrendPoint, tag_key};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashSet};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, MutexGuard};
use std::thread::JoinHandle;
use std::time::Duration;
use thiserror::Error;

pub type TransportFactory = Arc<dyn Fn(&LinkConfig) -> Result<Box<dyn Transport>, TransportError> + Send + Sync>;

const HUB_PERIOD_MS: u64 = 50;
const FLUSH_PERIOD_MS: u64 = 1000;

#[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum SessionError {
    #[error("unknown link '{0}'")]
    UnknownLink(String),
    #[error("unknown device '{0}'")]
    UnknownDevice(String),
    #[error("unknown profile '{0}'")]
    UnknownProfile(String),
    #[error("link id '{0}' already exists")]
    LinkExists(String),
    #[error("'{0}' is already in use by another link (one master per bus)")]
    BusOwned(String),
    #[error("device id '{0}' already exists")]
    DeviceExists(String),
    #[error("unit ID {0} is already used on this link")]
    UnitTaken(u8),
    #[error("link '{0}' is not connected")]
    NotConnected(String),
    #[error("{0}")]
    Device(DeviceError),
    #[error("cannot open link: {0}")]
    Transport(TransportError),
    #[error("invalid settings: {0}")]
    Settings(String),
    #[error("{0}")]
    Scheduler(SchedulerError),
    #[error("historian unavailable: {0}")]
    Historian(String),
    #[error("export failed: {0}")]
    Export(String),
    #[error("{0}")]
    Alarm(AlarmError),
    #[error("could not start the link worker: {0}")]
    Spawn(String),
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct SessionConfig {
    /// `None` = in-memory historian (tests).
    pub db_path: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub app_version: String,
    pub platform: String,
    pub logging_interval_ms: u64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum LinkState {
    /// Port open, not polling.
    Connected,
    Polling,
    /// The transport failed; the user must reconnect.
    Down,
    Disconnected,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ExportFormat {
    Csv,
    Xlsx,
    Json,
}

impl ExportFormat {
    pub fn extension(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ExportFormat::Csv => "csv",
            ExportFormat::Xlsx => "xlsx",
            ExportFormat::Json => "json",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct DeviceView {
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub link_id: String,
    pub unit_id: u8,
    pub profile_id: String,
    pub profile_version: String,
    pub simulated_only: bool,
    pub poll_interval_ms: u64,
    pub stale_after_ms: u64,
    pub counters: DeviceCounters,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct LinkView {
    pub id: String,
    /// `rtu`, `tcp`, `rtu_over_tcp`, `simulator`
    pub kind: &'static str,
    pub label: String,
    pub simulated: bool,
    pub state: LinkState,
    pub error: Option<String>,
    pub devices: Vec<DeviceView>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct LiveSnapshot {
    pub ts_ms: i64,
    pub session_id: String,
    pub tags: Vec<TagView>,
    pub links: Vec<LinkView>,
    pub alarms: AlarmSnapshot,
    pub historian_error: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct LiveFrame {
    pub ts_ms: i64,
    pub tags: Vec<TagView>,
    pub points: Vec<TrendPoint>,
    /// Points that could not be delivered (frame cap or bus lag). Never silent.
    pub dropped: u64,
    pub links: Option<Vec<LinkView>>,
    pub alarms: Option<AlarmSnapshot>,
    pub historian_error: Option<String>,
}

impl LiveFrame {
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.tags.is_empty()
            && self.points.is_empty()
            && self.dropped == 0
            && self.links.is_none()
            && self.alarms.is_none()
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct OrderValue {
    pub order: &'static str,
    pub value: Option<String>,
    pub error: Option<String>,
    pub is_profile: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct InspectRow {
    pub tag_id: String,
    pub name: Text,
    pub table: &'static str,
    pub doc_address: String,
    pub pdu_offset: u16,
    pub function: u8,
    pub function_name: &'static str,
    pub type_name: TypeName,
    pub word_order: Option<&'static str>,
    pub width: u16,
    pub unit: Option<String>,
    pub raw: Option<Vec<u16>>,
    pub raw_hex: Option<String>,
    /// Decoded raw value in the profile's word order.
    pub decoded: Option<String>,
    pub value: Option<f64>,
    /// All four orders for 32/64-bit types.
    pub orders: Vec<OrderValue>,
    pub quality: Option<&'static str>,
    pub exception: Option<u8>,
    pub exception_name: Option<&'static str>,
    pub error: Option<String>,
    pub value_ts_ms: Option<i64>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct DeviceInspection {
    pub device: DeviceView,
    pub rows: Vec<InspectRow>,
    pub frames: Vec<FrameEntry>,
}

struct LinkEntry {
    config: LinkConfig,
    simulated: bool,
    transport: Option<Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn Transport>>>>,
    devices: Vec<(DeviceInstance, Arc<Profile>)>,
    worker: Option<LinkWorker>,
    state: LinkState,
    error: Option<String>,
    counters: Vec<(String, DeviceCounters)>,
}

struct LogState {
    decimator: LogDecimator,
    batcher: SampleBatcher,
}

struct FrameCursor {
    alarm_rev: u64,
    links_rev: u64,
}

struct Shared {
    clock: Arc<dyn Clock>,
    factory: TransportFactory,
    registry: Arc<LinkRegistry>,
    bus: SampleBus,
    /// Global sequence; locked around publish so bus order equals sequence order.
    publish_lock: Arc<Mutex<u64>>,
    session_id: String,
    app_version: String,
    profiles: Mutex<BTreeMap<String, Arc<Profile>>>,
    links: Mutex<BTreeMap<String, LinkEntry>>,
    live: Mutex<LiveStore>,
    alarms: Mutex<AlarmEngine>,
    frames: Arc<Mutex<FrameLog>>,
    log: Mutex<LogState>,
    historian: Option<Mutex<Historian>>,
    historian_error: Mutex<Option<String>>,
    registered: Mutex<HashSet<String>>,
    links_rev: AtomicU64,
    cursor: Mutex<FrameCursor>,
    stop: AtomicBool,
}

fn lock<T>(m: &Mutex<T>) -> MutexGuard<'_, T> {
    m.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

/// Transport handed to a worker: delegates to the link's open transport and
/// does not close it, so the worker can be restarted without reopening the port.
struct SharedTransport(Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn Transport>>>);

impl Transport for SharedTransport {
    fn write_all(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
        lock(&self.0).write_all(bytes)
    }
    fn read(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8], timeout_ms: u64) -> Result<usize, TransportError> {
        lock(&self.0).read(buf, timeout_ms)
    }
    fn drain(&mut self, quiet_ms: u64) -> Result<usize, TransportError> {
        lock(&self.0).drain(quiet_ms)
    }
    fn close(&mut self) {}
}

fn publish_with(lock_seq: &Mutex<u64>, bus: &SampleBus, mut s: Sample) {
    let mut seq = lock(lock_seq);
    *seq += 1;
    s.seq = *seq;
    bus.publish(s);
}

fn link_kind(c: &LinkConfig) -> &'static str {
    match c.kind {
        LinkKind::Rtu { .. } => "rtu",
        LinkKind::Tcp { .. } => "tcp",
        LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { .. } => "rtu_over_tcp",
        LinkKind::Simulator { .. } => "simulator",
    }
}

fn serial_label(s: &crate::protocol::rtu::SerialSettings) -> String {
    let p = match s.parity {
        crate::protocol::rtu::Parity::None => 'N',
        crate::protocol::rtu::Parity::Even => 'E',
        crate::protocol::rtu::Parity::Odd => 'O',
    };
    format!("{} {}{}{}", s.baud, s.data_bits, p, s.stop_bits)
}

fn link_label(c: &LinkConfig) -> String {
    match &c.kind {
        LinkKind::Rtu { port, serial } => format!("{port} {}", serial_label(serial)),
        LinkKind::Tcp { host, port } => format!("{host}:{port}"),
        LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { host, port, serial } => format!("{host}:{port} RTU {}", serial_label(serial)),
        LinkKind::Simulator { name, serial } => format!("{name} {}", serial_label(serial)),
    }
}

impl Shared {
    fn now(&self) -> i64 {
        self.clock.utc_ms()
    }

    fn set_historian_error(&self, e: impl ToString) {
        *lock(&self.historian_error) = Some(e.to_string());
    }

    fn event(&self, kind: &str, device: Option<&str>, tag: Option<&str>, severity: &str, text: String) {
        let Some(h) = &self.historian else { return };
        let row = EventRow {
            session: Some(self.session_id.clone()),
            ts_ms: self.now(),
            kind: kind.to_owned(),
            device: device.map(str::to_owned),
            tag: tag.map(str::to_owned),
            severity: severity.to_owned(),
            text,
        };
        if let Err(e) = lock(h).add_event(&row) {
            self.set_historian_error(e);
        }
    }

    fn alarm_events_to_historian(&self, events: Vec<AlarmEvent>) {
        let Some(h) = &self.historian else { return };
        let mut h = lock(h);
        for ev in events {
            let row = EventRow {
                session: Some(self.session_id.clone()),
                ts_ms: ev.ts_ms,
                kind: "alarm".into(),
                device: Some(ev.device_id),
                tag: ev.tag_id,
                severity: format!("P{}", ev.priority),
                text: format!("{}: {}", ev.event, ev.text),
            };
            if let Err(e) = h.add_event(&row) {
                drop(h);
                self.set_historian_error(e);
                return;
            }
        }
    }

    fn store_batch(&self, batch: Vec<Sample>) {
        if batch.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let Some(h) = &self.historian else { return };
        if let Err(e) = lock(h).insert_samples(&batch) {
            self.set_historian_error(e);
        }
    }

    fn ingest(&self, s: &Arc<Sample>) {
        let now = self.now();
        lock(&self.live).apply(s);
        lock(&self.alarms).observe(s, now);
        let batch = {
            let mut log = lock(&self.log);
            if log.decimator.keep(s) {
                log.batcher.push((**s).clone(), now)
            } else {
                None
            }
        };
        if let Some(b) = batch {
            self.store_batch(b);
        }
    }

    fn flush_log(&self) {
        let batch = lock(&self.log).batcher.flush();
        self.store_batch(batch);
    }

    fn sink(&self) -> SampleSink {
        let bus = self.bus.clone();
        let seq = Arc::clone(&self.publish_lock);
        Arc::new(move |s: Sample| publish_with(&seq, &bus, s))
    }

    fn tap(&self, link_id: &str) -> FrameTap {
        let frames = Arc::clone(&self.frames);
        let clock = Arc::clone(&self.clock);
        let link = link_id.to_owned();
        Arc::new(move |rec| lock(&frames).push(&link, rec, clock.utc_ms()))
    }

    fn bump_links(&self) {
        self.links_rev.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
    }

    fn spawn_worker(&self, e: &mut LinkEntry) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let transport = e
            .transport
            .clone()
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::NotConnected(e.config.id.clone()))?;
        let mut sched = LinkScheduler::new(e.config.clone(), e.devices.clone(), Arc::clone(&self.clock))
            .map_err(SessionError::Scheduler)?;
        sched.set_frame_tap(self.tap(&e.config.id));
        let key = e.config.owner_key();
        let claim = self.registry.claim(&key).map_err(|_| SessionError::BusOwned(key))?;
        let worker = LinkWorker::spawn(claim, sched, Box::new(SharedTransport(transport)), self.sink())
            .map_err(|err| SessionError::Spawn(err.to_string()))?;
        e.worker = Some(worker);
        e.state = LinkState::Polling;
        e.error = None;
        self.bump_links();
        Ok(())
    }

    fn stop_worker(&self, e: &mut LinkEntry) {
        if let Some(w) = e.worker.take() {
            let st = w.stop();
            e.counters = st.counters;
        }
    }

    fn device_view(&self, e: &LinkEntry, d: &DeviceInstance, p: &Profile) -> DeviceView {
        let live = e.worker.as_ref().map(|w| w.status().counters);
        let counters = live
            .as_ref()
            .unwrap_or(&e.counters)
            .iter()
            .find(|(id, _)| *id == d.id)
            .map(|(_, c)| c.clone())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        DeviceView {
            id: d.id.clone(),
            name: d.name.clone(),
            link_id: d.link_id.clone(),
            unit_id: d.unit_id,
            profile_id: d.profile_id.clone(),
            profile_version: d.profile_version.clone(),
            simulated_only: p.simulated_only,
            poll_interval_ms: d.poll_interval_ms,
            stale_after_ms: d.stale_threshold_ms(),
            counters,
        }
    }

    fn link_views(&self, links: &BTreeMap<String, LinkEntry>) -> Vec<LinkView> {
        links
            .values()
            .map(|e| LinkView {
                id: e.config.id.clone(),
                kind: link_kind(&e.config),
                label: link_label(&e.config),
                simulated: e.simulated,
                state: e.state,
                error: e.error.clone(),
                devices: e.devices.iter().map(|(d, p)| self.device_view(e, d, p)).collect(),
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Hub: a worker that died with its transport → link Down (never restarted here).
    fn check_links(&self) {
        let mut down = Vec::new();
        {
            let mut links = lock(&self.links);
            for e in links.values_mut() {
                let finished = e.worker.as_ref().is_some_and(|w| w.is_finished());
                if !finished {
                    continue;
                }
                if let Some(w) = e.worker.take() {
                    let st = w.stop();
                    e.counters = st.counters.clone();
                    if st.state == WorkerState::Down {
                        let why = st
                            .counters
                            .iter()
                            .find_map(|(_, c)| c.last_error.clone())
                            .unwrap_or_else(|| "transport lost".into());
                        e.state = LinkState::Down;
                        e.error = Some(why.clone());
                        if let Some(t) = e.transport.take() {
                            lock(&t).close();
                        }
                        down.push((e.config.id.clone(), why));
                    } else {
                        e.state = LinkState::Connected;
                    }
                    self.bump_links();
                }
            }
        }
        for (id, why) in down {
            self.event("link", None, None, "warning", format!("link {id} down: {why}"));
        }
    }
}

fn hub(shared: Arc<Shared>, mut sub: crate::bus::BusSubscriber) {
    let mut last_flush = shared.clock.mono_ms();
    loop {
        let stopping = shared.stop.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
        for r in sub.drain() {
            match r {
                BusRecv::Sample(s) => shared.ingest(&s),
                BusRecv::Lagged(n) => lock(&shared.live).add_dropped(n),
                BusRecv::Empty | BusRecv::Closed => {}
            }
        }
        let now = shared.now();
        let events = {
            let mut a = lock(&shared.alarms);
            a.tick(now);
            a.take_events()
        };
        shared.alarm_events_to_historian(events);
        let mono = shared.clock.mono_ms();
        if stopping || mono.saturating_sub(last_flush) >= FLUSH_PERIOD_MS {
            last_flush = mono;
            shared.flush_log();
            shared.check_links();
        }
        if stopping {
            break;
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(HUB_PERIOD_MS));
    }
}

fn lock<T>(m: &Mutex<T>) -> MutexGuard<'_, T> {
    m.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

/// Transport handed to a worker: delegates to the link's open transport and
/// does not close it, so the worker can be restarted without reopening the port.
struct SharedTransport(Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn Transport>>>);

impl Transport for SharedTransport {
    fn write_all(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
        lock(&self.0).write_all(bytes)
    }
    fn read(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8], timeout_ms: u64) -> Result<usize, TransportError> {
        lock(&self.0).read(buf, timeout_ms)
    }
    fn drain(&mut self, quiet_ms: u64) -> Result<usize, TransportError> {
        lock(&self.0).drain(quiet_ms)
    }
    fn close(&mut self) {}
}

fn publish_with(lock_seq: &Mutex<u64>, bus: &SampleBus, mut s: Sample) {
    let mut seq = lock(lock_seq);
    *seq += 1;
    s.seq = *seq;
    bus.publish(s);
}

fn link_kind(c: &LinkConfig) -> &'static str {
    match c.kind {
        LinkKind::Rtu { .. } => "rtu",
        LinkKind::Tcp { .. } => "tcp",
        LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { .. } => "rtu_over_tcp",
        LinkKind::Simulator { .. } => "simulator",
    }
}

fn serial_label(s: &crate::protocol::rtu::SerialSettings) -> String {
    let p = match s.parity {
        crate::protocol::rtu::Parity::None => 'N',
        crate::protocol::rtu::Parity::Even => 'E',
        crate::protocol::rtu::Parity::Odd => 'O',
    };
    format!("{} {}{}{}", s.baud, s.data_bits, p, s.stop_bits)
}

fn link_label(c: &LinkConfig) -> String {
    match &c.kind {
        LinkKind::Rtu { port, serial } => format!("{port} {}", serial_label(serial)),
        LinkKind::Tcp { host, port } => format!("{host}:{port}"),
        LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { host, port, serial } => format!("{host}:{port} RTU {}", serial_label(serial)),
        LinkKind::Simulator { name, serial } => format!("{name} {}", serial_label(serial)),
    }
}

impl Shared {
    fn now(&self) -> i64 {
        self.clock.utc_ms()
    }

    fn set_historian_error(&self, e: impl ToString) {
        *lock(&self.historian_error) = Some(e.to_string());
    }

    fn event(&self, kind: &str, device: Option<&str>, tag: Option<&str>, severity: &str, text: String) {
        let Some(h) = &self.historian else { return };
        let row = EventRow {
            session: Some(self.session_id.clone()),
            ts_ms: self.now(),
            kind: kind.to_owned(),
            device: device.map(str::to_owned),
            tag: tag.map(str::to_owned),
            severity: severity.to_owned(),
            text,
        };
        if let Err(e) = lock(h).add_event(&row) {
            self.set_historian_error(e);
        }
    }

    fn alarm_events_to_historian(&self, events: Vec<AlarmEvent>) {
        let Some(h) = &self.historian else { return };
        let mut h = lock(h);
        for ev in events {
            let row = EventRow {
                session: Some(self.session_id.clone()),
                ts_ms: ev.ts_ms,
                kind: "alarm".into(),
                device: Some(ev.device_id),
                tag: ev.tag_id,
                severity: format!("P{}", ev.priority),
                text: format!("{}: {}", ev.event, ev.text),
            };
            if let Err(e) = h.add_event(&row) {
                drop(h);
                self.set_historian_error(e);
                return;
            }
        }
    }

    fn store_batch(&self, batch: Vec<Sample>) {
        if batch.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let Some(h) = &self.historian else { return };
        if let Err(e) = lock(h).insert_samples(&batch) {
            self.set_historian_error(e);
        }
    }

    fn ingest(&self, s: &Arc<Sample>) {
        let now = self.now();
        lock(&self.live).apply(s);
        lock(&self.alarms).observe(s, now);
        let batch = {
            let mut log = lock(&self.log);
            if log.decimator.keep(s) {
                log.batcher.push((**s).clone(), now)
            } else {
                None
            }
        };
        if let Some(b) = batch {
            self.store_batch(b);
        }
    }

    fn flush_log(&self) {
        let batch = lock(&self.log).batcher.flush();
        self.store_batch(batch);
    }

    fn sink(&self) -> SampleSink {
        let bus = self.bus.clone();
        let seq = Arc::clone(&self.publish_lock);
        Arc::new(move |s: Sample| publish_with(&seq, &bus, s))
    }

    fn tap(&self, link_id: &str) -> FrameTap {
        let frames = Arc::clone(&self.frames);
        let clock = Arc::clone(&self.clock);
        let link = link_id.to_owned();
        Arc::new(move |rec| lock(&frames).push(&link, rec, clock.utc_ms()))
    }

    fn bump_links(&self) {
        self.links_rev.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
    }

    fn spawn_worker(&self, e: &mut LinkEntry) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let transport = e
            .transport
            .clone()
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::NotConnected(e.config.id.clone()))?;
        let mut sched = LinkScheduler::new(e.config.clone(), e.devices.clone(), Arc::clone(&self.clock))
            .map_err(SessionError::Scheduler)?;
        sched.set_frame_tap(self.tap(&e.config.id));
        let key = e.config.owner_key();
        let claim = self.registry.claim(&key).map_err(|_| SessionError::BusOwned(key))?;
        let worker = LinkWorker::spawn(claim, sched, Box::new(SharedTransport(transport)), self.sink())
            .map_err(|err| SessionError::Spawn(err.to_string()))?;
        e.worker = Some(worker);
        e.state = LinkState::Polling;
        e.error = None;
        self.bump_links();
        Ok(())
    }

    fn stop_worker(&self, e: &mut LinkEntry) {
        if let Some(w) = e.worker.take() {
            let st = w.stop();
            e.counters = st.counters;
        }
    }

    fn device_view(&self, e: &LinkEntry, d: &DeviceInstance, p: &Profile) -> DeviceView {
        let live = e.worker.as_ref().map(|w| w.status().counters);
        let counters = live
            .as_ref()
            .unwrap_or(&e.counters)
            .iter()
            .find(|(id, _)| *id == d.id)
            .map(|(_, c)| c.clone())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        DeviceView {
            id: d.id.clone(),
            name: d.name.clone(),
            link_id: d.link_id.clone(),
            unit_id: d.unit_id,
            profile_id: d.profile_id.clone(),
            profile_version: d.profile_version.clone(),
            simulated_only: p.simulated_only,
            poll_interval_ms: d.poll_interval_ms,
            stale_after_ms: d.stale_threshold_ms(),
            counters,
        }
    }

    fn link_views(&self, links: &BTreeMap<String, LinkEntry>) -> Vec<LinkView> {
        links
            .values()
            .map(|e| LinkView {
                id: e.config.id.clone(),
                kind: link_kind(&e.config),
                label: link_label(&e.config),
                simulated: e.simulated,
                state: e.state,
                error: e.error.clone(),
                devices: e.devices.iter().map(|(d, p)| self.device_view(e, d, p)).collect(),
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Hub: a worker that died with its transport → link Down (never restarted here).
    fn check_links(&self) {
        let mut down = Vec::new();
        {
            let mut links = lock(&self.links);
            for e in links.values_mut() {
                let finished = e.worker.as_ref().is_some_and(|w| w.is_finished());
                if !finished {
                    continue;
                }
                if let Some(w) = e.worker.take() {
                    let st = w.stop();
                    e.counters = st.counters.clone();
                    if st.state == WorkerState::Down {
                        let why = st
                            .counters
                            .iter()
                            .find_map(|(_, c)| c.last_error.clone())
                            .unwrap_or_else(|| "transport lost".into());
                        e.state = LinkState::Down;
                        e.error = Some(why.clone());
                        if let Some(t) = e.transport.take() {
                            lock(&t).close();
                        }
                        down.push((e.config.id.clone(), why));
                    } else {
                        e.state = LinkState::Connected;
                    }
                    self.bump_links();
                }
            }
        }
        for (id, why) in down {
            self.event("link", None, None, "warning", format!("link {id} down: {why}"));
        }
    }
}

fn hub(shared: Arc<Shared>, mut sub: crate::bus::BusSubscriber) {
    let mut last_flush = shared.clock.mono_ms();
    loop {
        let stopping = shared.stop.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
        for r in sub.drain() {
            match r {
                BusRecv::Sample(s) => shared.ingest(&s),
                BusRecv::Lagged(n) => lock(&shared.live).add_dropped(n),
                BusRecv::Empty | BusRecv::Closed => {}
            }
        }
        let now = shared.now();
        let events = {
            let mut a = lock(&shared.alarms);
            a.tick(now);
            a.take_events()
        };
        shared.alarm_events_to_historian(events);
        let mono = shared.clock.mono_ms();
        if stopping || mono.saturating_sub(last_flush) >= FLUSH_PERIOD_MS {
            last_flush = mono;
            shared.flush_log();
            shared.check_links();
        }
        if stopping {
            break;
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(HUB_PERIOD_MS));
    }
}

        lock(&self.shared.profiles).insert(key.clone(), Arc::new(p));

    }

    /// Open a new link (Monitoring: nothing is polled until `start_polling`).
    pub fn connect(&self, config: LinkConfig, simulated: bool) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        if let Some(s) = config.serial() {
            s.validate().map_err(|e| SessionError::Settings(e.into()))?;
        }
        let id_ok = (1..=48).contains(&config.id.len())
            && config
                .id
                .bytes()
                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || matches!(c, b'-' | b'_'));
        if !id_ok {
            return Err(SessionError::Settings(
                "link id must be 1-48 of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_'".into(),
            ));
        }
        if simulated != config.is_simulator() {
            return Err(SessionError::Settings("only simulator links can be simulated".into()));
        }
        let key = config.owner_key();
        let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        if links.contains_key(&config.id) {
            return Err(SessionError::LinkExists(config.id));
        }
        let open_with_key = links
            .values()
            .any(|e| e.transport.is_some() && e.config.owner_key() == key);
        if open_with_key || self.shared.registry.is_owned(&key) {
            return Err(SessionError::BusOwned(key));
        }
        let transport = (self.shared.factory)(&config).map_err(SessionError::Transport)?;
        let id = config.id.clone();
        links.insert(
            id.clone(),
            LinkEntry {
                config,
                simulated,
                transport: Some(Arc::new(Mutex::new(transport))),
                devices: Vec::new(),
                worker: None,
                state: LinkState::Connected,
                error: None,
                counters: Vec::new(),
            },
        );
        drop(links);
        self.shared.bump_links();
        self.shared
            .event("link", None, None, "info", format!("link {id} connected"));
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reopen a disconnected or failed link with its stored settings. It comes
    /// back in Monitoring (connected, not polling): reconnect never restarts anything.
    pub fn reconnect(&self, link_id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        let key = {
            let e = links
                .get(link_id)
                .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::UnknownLink(link_id.into()))?;
            if e.transport.is_some() {
                return Ok(());
            }
            e.config.owner_key()
        };
        let busy = links
            .values()
            .any(|o| o.config.id != link_id && o.transport.is_some() && o.config.owner_key() == key);
        if busy || self.shared.registry.is_owned(&key) {
            return Err(SessionError::BusOwned(key));
        }
        let Some(e) = links.get_mut(link_id) else {
            return Err(SessionError::UnknownLink(link_id.into()));
        };
        let t = (self.shared.factory)(&e.config).map_err(SessionError::Transport)?;
        e.transport = Some(Arc::new(Mutex::new(t)));
        e.state = LinkState::Connected;
        e.error = None;
        drop(links);
        self.shared.bump_links();
        self.shared
            .event("link", None, None, "info", format!("link {link_id} reconnected"));
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Stop polling, close the port and mark every tag of the link DISCONNECTED
    /// (last good value and its time kept).
    pub fn disconnect(&self, link_id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        {
            let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
            let e = links
                .get_mut(link_id)
                .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::UnknownLink(link_id.into()))?;
            self.shared.stop_worker(e);
            if let Some(t) = e.transport.take() {
                lock(&t).close();
            }
            e.state = LinkState::Disconnected;
        }
        self.shared.bump_links();
        self.publish_disconnected(link_id, "disconnected by the user");
        self.shared
            .event("link", None, None, "info", format!("link {link_id} disconnected"));
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Disconnect (if needed) and forget a link and its devices.
    pub fn remove_link(&self, link_id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        self.disconnect(link_id)?;
        let removed = lock(&self.shared.links).remove(link_id);
        if let Some(e) = removed {
            let mut live = lock(&self.shared.live);
            let mut alarms = lock(&self.shared.alarms);
            for (d, _) in &e.devices {
                live.remove_device(&d.id);
                alarms.remove_device(&d.id);
            }
        }
        lock(&self.shared.frames).clear_link(link_id);
        self.shared.bump_links();
        Ok(())
    }

    fn publish_disconnected(&self, link_id: &str, why: &str) {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        let last = lock(&self.shared.live).last_samples_of_link(link_id);
        for s in last {
            if s.quality == Quality::Disconnected {
                continue;
            }
            let mut d = (*s).clone();
            d.quality = Quality::Disconnected;
            d.ts_ms = now;
            d.age_ms = d.value_ts_ms.map(|t| u64::try_from(now.saturating_sub(t)).unwrap_or(0));
            d.raw = None;
            d.error = Some(why.to_owned());
            publish_with(&self.shared.publish_lock, &self.shared.bus, d);
        }
    }

    pub fn start_polling(&self, link_id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        let e = links
            .get_mut(link_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::UnknownLink(link_id.into()))?;
        match e.state {
            LinkState::Polling => Ok(()),
            LinkState::Connected => self.shared.spawn_worker(e),
            LinkState::Down | LinkState::Disconnected => Err(SessionError::NotConnected(link_id.into())),
        }
    }

    pub fn stop_polling(&self, link_id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        let e = links
            .get_mut(link_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::UnknownLink(link_id.into()))?;
        if e.state == LinkState::Polling {
            self.shared.stop_worker(e);
            e.state = LinkState::Connected;
            self.shared.bump_links();
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// A free device id derived from the profile and unit ID.
    pub fn suggest_device_id(&self, profile_id: &str, unit: u8) -> String {
        let base: String = profile_id
            .chars()
            .map(|c| {
                if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
                    c.to_ascii_lowercase()
                } else {
                    '-'
                }
            })
            .collect();
        let base = format!("{}-u{unit}", base.trim_matches('-'));
        let taken: HashSet<String> = lock(&self.shared.links)
            .values()
            .flat_map(|e| e.devices.iter().map(|(d, _)| d.id.clone()))
            .collect();
        if !taken.contains(&base) {
            return base;
        }
        (2..)
            .map(|n| format!("{base}-{n}"))
            .find(|c| !taken.contains(c))
            .unwrap_or(base)
    }

            return Err(SessionError::UnitTaken(d.unit_id));
        }
        e.devices.push((d.clone(), Arc::clone(&profile)));
        if e.state == LinkState::Polling {
            self.shared.stop_worker(e);
            if let Err(err) = self.shared.spawn_worker(e) {
                e.devices.pop();
                e.state = LinkState::Connected;
                let _ = self.shared.spawn_worker(e);
                return Err(err);
            }
        }
        let link = link_label(&e.config);
        drop(links);
        self.shared.bump_links();
        self.register_device(&d, &link);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn register_device(&self, d: &DeviceInstance, link: &str) {
        let Some(h) = &self.shared.historian else { return };
        if !lock(&self.shared.registered).insert(d.id.clone()) {
            return;
        }
        let row = DeviceRow {
            session: self.shared.session_id.clone(),
            device_id: d.id.clone(),
            name: d.name.clone(),
            profile_id: d.profile_id.clone(),
            profile_version: d.profile_version.clone(),
            unit_id: d.unit_id,
            link: link.to_owned(),
        };
        if let Err(e) = lock(h).register_device(&row) {
            self.shared.set_historian_error(e);
        }
    }

    pub fn remove_device(&self, device_id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        let e = links
            .values_mut()
            .find(|e| e.devices.iter().any(|(d, _)| d.id == device_id))
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::UnknownDevice(device_id.into()))?;
        e.devices.retain(|(d, _)| d.id != device_id);
        if e.state == LinkState::Polling {
            self.shared.stop_worker(e);
            self.shared.spawn_worker(e)?;
        }
        drop(links);
        lock(&self.shared.live).remove_device(device_id);
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).remove_device(device_id);
        self.shared.bump_links();
        Ok(())
    }

    fn find_device(&self, device_id: &str) -> Result<(DeviceInstance, Arc<Profile>, DeviceView), SessionError> {
        let links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        for e in links.values() {
            if let Some((d, p)) = e.devices.iter().find(|(d, _)| d.id == device_id) {
                let view = self.shared.device_view(e, d, p);
                return Ok((d.clone(), Arc::clone(p), view));
            }
        }
        Err(SessionError::UnknownDevice(device_id.into()))
    }

    // ---- live ----

    pub fn links(&self) -> Vec<LinkView> {
        let links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        self.shared.link_views(&links)
    }

    pub fn link_config(&self, link_id: &str) -> Option<LinkConfig> {
        lock(&self.shared.links).get(link_id).map(|e| e.config.clone())
    }

    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> LiveSnapshot {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        let links = self.links();
        LiveSnapshot {
            ts_ms: now,
            session_id: self.shared.session_id.clone(),
            tags: lock(&self.shared.live).all(),
            links,
            alarms: lock(&self.shared.alarms).snapshot(now),
            historian_error: lock(&self.shared.historian_error).clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Changes since the last call (the shell calls this at ≤ 4 Hz).
    pub fn take_frame(&self) -> LiveFrame {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        let links_rev = self.shared.links_rev.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
        let alarm_rev = lock(&self.shared.alarms).revision();
        let (send_links, send_alarms) = {
            let mut c = lock(&self.shared.cursor);
            let l = c.links_rev != links_rev;
            let a = c.alarm_rev != alarm_rev;
            c.links_rev = links_rev;
            c.alarm_rev = alarm_rev;
            (l, a)
        };
        let links = send_links.then(|| self.links());
        let (tags, points, dropped) = lock(&self.shared.live).take_changes();
        let alarms = send_alarms.then(|| lock(&self.shared.alarms).snapshot(now));
        LiveFrame {
            ts_ms: now,
            tags,
            points,
            dropped,
            links,
            alarms,
            historian_error: lock(&self.shared.historian_error).clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Link views with fresh counters (heartbeat); counters change without a link revision.
    pub fn link_status(&self) -> Vec<LinkView> {
        self.links()
    }

    // ---- historian ----

    pub fn flush(&self) {
        self.shared.flush_log();
    }

    pub fn sessions(&self) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>, SessionError> {
        let h = self
            .shared
            .historian
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::Historian(self.historian_error_text()))?;
        lock(h).sessions().map_err(|e| SessionError::Historian(e.to_string()))
    }

    fn historian_error_text(&self) -> String {
        lock(&self.shared.historian_error)
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "not opened".into())
    }

    pub fn trend(
        &self,
        device_id: &str,
        tag_id: &str,
        from_ms: i64,
        to_ms: i64,
        buckets: usize,
    ) -> Result<TrendSeries, SessionError> {
        let (d, _, _) = self.find_device(device_id)?;
        self.shared.flush_log();
        let h = self
            .shared
            .historian
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::Historian(self.historian_error_text()))?;
        let rows = lock(h)
            .samples(&self.shared.session_id, Some(device_id), Some(tag_id), from_ms, to_ms)
            .map_err(|e| SessionError::Historian(e.to_string()))?;
        let input: Vec<TrendInput> = rows
            .iter()
            .map(|s| TrendInput {
                ts_ms: s.ts_ms,
                value: s.value,
                quality: s.quality,
            })
            .collect();
        Ok(trend::decimate(&input, from_ms, to_ms, buckets, d.stale_threshold_ms()))
    }

    pub fn export(&self, format: ExportFormat) -> Result<Vec<u8>, SessionError> {
        self.shared.flush_log();
        let h = self
            .shared
            .historian
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::Historian(self.historian_error_text()))?;
        let doc = ExportDoc::from_historian(
            &lock(h),
            &self.shared.session_id,
            self.shared.now(),
            &self.shared.app_version,
        )
        .map_err(|e| SessionError::Export(e.to_string()))?;
        match format {
            ExportFormat::Csv => Ok(export::csv::measurements(&doc).into_bytes()),
            ExportFormat::Json => Ok(export::json::to_string(&doc).into_bytes()),
            ExportFormat::Xlsx => export::xlsx::workbook(&doc).map_err(|e| SessionError::Export(e.to_string())),
        }
    }

    pub fn events(&self, kind: Option<&str>, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<EventRow>, SessionError> {
        let h = self
            .shared
            .historian
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::Historian(self.historian_error_text()))?;
        let mut rows = lock(h)
            .events(&self.shared.session_id)
            .map_err(|e| SessionError::Historian(e.to_string()))?;
        if let Some(k) = kind {
            rows.retain(|r| r.kind == k);
        }
        let skip = rows.len().saturating_sub(limit);
        Ok(rows.split_off(skip))
    }

    // ---- inspector ----

    pub fn inspect(&self, device_id: &str) -> Result<DeviceInspection, SessionError> {
        let (d, p, view) = self.find_device(device_id)?;
        let live = lock(&self.shared.live);
        let rows = p
            .registers
            .iter()
            .map(|r| {
                let key = tag_key(&d.id, &r.id);
                let tv = live.get(&key);
                let raw = live.last_raw(&key).map(<[u16]>::to_vec);
                let dt = r.data_type();
                let decoded = match (&raw, dt) {
                    (Some(words), Some(dt)) => codec::decode(dt, r.word_order, words).ok().map(|v| v.display()),
                    _ => None,
                };
                let orders = match (&raw, dt) {
                    (Some(words), Some(dt)) if r.type_name.needs_word_order() => codec::decode_all_orders(dt, words)
                        .into_iter()
                        .map(|(o, res)| OrderValue {
                            order: o.as_str(),
                            is_profile: r.word_order == Some(o),
                            value: res.as_ref().ok().map(|v| v.display()),
                            error: res.err().map(|e| e.to_string()),
                        })
                        .collect(),
                    _ => Vec::new(),
                };
                let f = r.table.read_function();
                InspectRow {
                    tag_id: r.id.clone(),
                    name: r.name.clone(),
                    table: r.table.as_str(),
                    doc_address: r.doc_label(),
                    pdu_offset: r.address,
                    function: f.code(),
                    function_name: f.name(),
                    type_name: r.type_name,
                    word_order: r.word_order.map(|o| o.as_str()),
                    width: r.width(),
                    unit: r.unit.clone(),
                    raw_hex: raw.as_deref().map(export::raw_hex),
                    raw,
                    decoded,
                    value: tv.and_then(|t| t.value),
                    orders,
                    quality: tv.map(|t| t.quality),
                    exception: tv.and_then(|t| t.exception),
                    exception_name: tv.and_then(|t| t.exception).map(|c| ExceptionCode(c).name()),
                    error: tv.and_then(|t| t.error.clone()),
                    value_ts_ms: tv.and_then(|t| t.value_ts_ms),
                }
            })
            .collect();
        drop(live);
        let frames = lock(&self.shared.frames).of(&d.link_id, d.unit_id);
        Ok(DeviceInspection {
            device: view,
            rows,
            frames,
        })
    }

    // ---- alarms ----

    pub fn alarm_add(&self, def: AlarmDef) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        self.find_device(&def.device_id)?;
        let now = self.shared.now();
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).add(def, now).map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarm_remove(&self, id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).remove(id).map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarm_ack(&self, id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).ack(id, now).map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarm_shelve(&self, id: &str, duration_ms: u64) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        let until = now.saturating_add(i64::try_from(duration_ms).unwrap_or(i64::MAX));
        lock(&self.shared.alarms)
            .shelve(id, until, now)
            .map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarm_unshelve(&self, id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).unshelve(id, now).map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarm_set_out_of_service(&self, id: &str, oos: bool) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        lock(&self.shared.alarms)
            .set_out_of_service(id, oos, now)
            .map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarms(&self) -> AlarmSnapshot {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).snapshot(now)
    }

    pub fn alarm_defs(&self) -> Vec<AlarmDef> {
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).defs()
    }

    /// Samples applied to the live store so far (diagnostics and tests).
    pub fn applied_samples(&self) -> u64 {
        lock(&self.shared.live).applied()
    }

    /// Stop every worker, flush the historian and end the hub thread.
    pub fn shutdown(&self) {
        {
            let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
            for e in links.values_mut() {
                self.shared.stop_worker(e);
                if let Some(t) = e.transport.take() {
                    lock(&t).close();
                }
                e.state = LinkState::Disconnected;
            }
        }
        self.shared.stop.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        if let Some(h) = lock(&self.hub).take() {
            let _ = h.join();
        }
        self.shared.flush_log();
    }
}

impl Drop for Session {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.shutdown();
    }
}

    // ---- links ----

    /// Open a new link (Monitoring: nothing is polled until `start_polling`).
    pub fn connect(&self, config: LinkConfig, simulated: bool) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        if let Some(s) = config.serial() {
            s.validate().map_err(|e| SessionError::Settings(e.into()))?;
        }
        let id_ok = (1..=48).contains(&config.id.len())
            && config
                .id
                .bytes()
                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || matches!(c, b'-' | b'_'));
        if !id_ok {
            return Err(SessionError::Settings(
                "link id must be 1-48 of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_'".into(),
            ));
        }
        if simulated != config.is_simulator() {
            return Err(SessionError::Settings("only simulator links can be simulated".into()));
        }
        let key = config.owner_key();
        let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        if links.contains_key(&config.id) {
            return Err(SessionError::LinkExists(config.id));
        }
        let open_with_key = links
            .values()
            .any(|e| e.transport.is_some() && e.config.owner_key() == key);
        if open_with_key || self.shared.registry.is_owned(&key) {
            return Err(SessionError::BusOwned(key));
        }
        let transport = (self.shared.factory)(&config).map_err(SessionError::Transport)?;
        let id = config.id.clone();
        links.insert(
            id.clone(),
            LinkEntry {
                config,
                simulated,
                transport: Some(Arc::new(Mutex::new(transport))),
                devices: Vec::new(),
                worker: None,
                state: LinkState::Connected,
                error: None,
                counters: Vec::new(),
            },
        );
        drop(links);
        self.shared.bump_links();
        self.shared
            .event("link", None, None, "info", format!("link {id} connected"));
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reopen a disconnected or failed link with its stored settings. It comes
    /// back in Monitoring (connected, not polling): reconnect never restarts anything.
    pub fn reconnect(&self, link_id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        let key = {
            let e = links
                .get(link_id)
                .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::UnknownLink(link_id.into()))?;
            if e.transport.is_some() {
                return Ok(());
            }
            e.config.owner_key()
        };
        let busy = links
            .values()
            .any(|o| o.config.id != link_id && o.transport.is_some() && o.config.owner_key() == key);
        if busy || self.shared.registry.is_owned(&key) {
            return Err(SessionError::BusOwned(key));
        }
        let Some(e) = links.get_mut(link_id) else {
            return Err(SessionError::UnknownLink(link_id.into()));
        };
        let t = (self.shared.factory)(&e.config).map_err(SessionError::Transport)?;
        e.transport = Some(Arc::new(Mutex::new(t)));
        e.state = LinkState::Connected;
        e.error = None;
        drop(links);
        self.shared.bump_links();
        self.shared
            .event("link", None, None, "info", format!("link {link_id} reconnected"));
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Stop polling, close the port and mark every tag of the link DISCONNECTED
    /// (last good value and its time kept).
    pub fn disconnect(&self, link_id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        {
            let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
            let e = links
                .get_mut(link_id)
                .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::UnknownLink(link_id.into()))?;
            self.shared.stop_worker(e);
            if let Some(t) = e.transport.take() {
                lock(&t).close();
            }
            e.state = LinkState::Disconnected;
        }
        self.shared.bump_links();
        self.publish_disconnected(link_id, "disconnected by the user");
        self.shared
            .event("link", None, None, "info", format!("link {link_id} disconnected"));
        Ok(())
    }

        if let Some(e) = removed {

            let mut alarms = lock(&self.shared.alarms);
            for (d, _) in &e.devices {
                live.remove_device(&d.id);

    /// A free device id derived from the profile and unit ID.
    pub fn suggest_device_id(&self, profile_id: &str, unit: u8) -> String {
        let base: String = profile_id
            .chars()
            .map(|c| {
                if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
                    c.to_ascii_lowercase()
                } else {
                    '-'
                }
            })
            .collect();
        let base = format!("{}-u{unit}", base.trim_matches('-'));
        let taken: HashSet<String> = lock(&self.shared.links)
            .values()
            .flat_map(|e| e.devices.iter().map(|(d, _)| d.id.clone()))
            .collect();

            return base;
        }

            .map(|n| format!("{base}-{n}"))
            .find(|c| !taken.contains(c))
            .unwrap_or(base)
    }
