        let e = links
            .values_mut()
            .find(|e| e.devices.iter().any(|(d, _)| d.id == device_id))
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::UnknownDevice(device_id.into()))?;
        e.devices.retain(|(d, _)| d.id != device_id);
        if e.state == LinkState::Polling {
            self.shared.stop_worker(e);
            self.shared.spawn_worker(e)?;
        }
        drop(links);
        lock(&self.shared.live).remove_device(device_id);
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).remove_device(device_id);
        self.shared.bump_links();
        Ok(())
    }

    fn find_device(&self, device_id: &str) -> Result<(DeviceInstance, Arc<Profile>, DeviceView), SessionError> {
        let links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        for e in links.values() {
            if let Some((d, p)) = e.devices.iter().find(|(d, _)| d.id == device_id) {
                let view = self.shared.device_view(e, d, p);
                return Ok((d.clone(), Arc::clone(p), view));
            }
        }
        Err(SessionError::UnknownDevice(device_id.into()))
    }

    // ---- live ----

    pub fn links(&self) -> Vec<LinkView> {
        let links = lock(&self.shared.links);
        self.shared.link_views(&links)
    }

    pub fn link_config(&self, link_id: &str) -> Option<LinkConfig> {
        lock(&self.shared.links).get(link_id).map(|e| e.config.clone())
    }

    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> LiveSnapshot {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        let links = self.links();
        LiveSnapshot {
            ts_ms: now,
            session_id: self.shared.session_id.clone(),
            tags: lock(&self.shared.live).all(),
            links,
            alarms: lock(&self.shared.alarms).snapshot(now),
            historian_error: lock(&self.shared.historian_error).clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Changes since the last call (the shell calls this at ≤ 4 Hz).
    pub fn take_frame(&self) -> LiveFrame {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        let links_rev = self.shared.links_rev.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
        let alarm_rev = lock(&self.shared.alarms).revision();
        let (send_links, send_alarms) = {
            let mut c = lock(&self.shared.cursor);
            let l = c.links_rev != links_rev;
            let a = c.alarm_rev != alarm_rev;
            c.links_rev = links_rev;
            c.alarm_rev = alarm_rev;
            (l, a)
        };
        let links = send_links.then(|| self.links());
        let (tags, points, dropped) = lock(&self.shared.live).take_changes();
        let alarms = send_alarms.then(|| lock(&self.shared.alarms).snapshot(now));
        LiveFrame {
            ts_ms: now,
            tags,
            points,
            dropped,
            links,
            alarms,
            historian_error: lock(&self.shared.historian_error).clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Link views with fresh counters (heartbeat); counters change without a link revision.
    pub fn link_status(&self) -> Vec<LinkView> {
        self.links()
    }

    // ---- historian ----

    pub fn flush(&self) {
        self.shared.flush_log();
    }

    pub fn sessions(&self) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>, SessionError> {
        let h = self
            .shared
            .historian
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::Historian(self.historian_error_text()))?;
        lock(h).sessions().map_err(|e| SessionError::Historian(e.to_string()))
    }

    fn historian_error_text(&self) -> String {
        lock(&self.shared.historian_error)
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "not opened".into())
    }

    pub fn trend(
        &self,
        device_id: &str,
        tag_id: &str,
        from_ms: i64,
        to_ms: i64,
        buckets: usize,
    ) -> Result<TrendSeries, SessionError> {
        let (d, _, _) = self.find_device(device_id)?;
        self.shared.flush_log();
        let h = self
            .shared
            .historian
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::Historian(self.historian_error_text()))?;
        let rows = lock(h)
            .samples(&self.shared.session_id, Some(device_id), Some(tag_id), from_ms, to_ms)
            .map_err(|e| SessionError::Historian(e.to_string()))?;
        let input: Vec<TrendInput> = rows
            .iter()
            .map(|s| TrendInput {
                ts_ms: s.ts_ms,
                value: s.value,
                quality: s.quality,
            })
            .collect();
        Ok(trend::decimate(&input, from_ms, to_ms, buckets, d.stale_threshold_ms()))
    }

    pub fn export(&self, format: ExportFormat) -> Result<Vec<u8>, SessionError> {
        self.shared.flush_log();
        let h = self
            .shared
            .historian
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::Historian(self.historian_error_text()))?;
        let doc = ExportDoc::from_historian(
            &lock(h),
            &self.shared.session_id,
            self.shared.now(),
            &self.shared.app_version,
        )
        .map_err(|e| SessionError::Export(e.to_string()))?;
        match format {
            ExportFormat::Csv => Ok(export::csv::measurements(&doc).into_bytes()),
            ExportFormat::Json => Ok(export::json::to_string(&doc).into_bytes()),
            ExportFormat::Xlsx => export::xlsx::workbook(&doc).map_err(|e| SessionError::Export(e.to_string())),
        }
    }

    pub fn events(&self, kind: Option<&str>, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<EventRow>, SessionError> {
        let h = self
            .shared
            .historian
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| SessionError::Historian(self.historian_error_text()))?;
        let mut rows = lock(h)
            .events(&self.shared.session_id)
            .map_err(|e| SessionError::Historian(e.to_string()))?;
        if let Some(k) = kind {
            rows.retain(|r| r.kind == k);
        }
        let skip = rows.len().saturating_sub(limit);
        Ok(rows.split_off(skip))
    }

    // ---- inspector ----

    pub fn inspect(&self, device_id: &str) -> Result<DeviceInspection, SessionError> {
        let (d, p, view) = self.find_device(device_id)?;
        let live = lock(&self.shared.live);
        let rows = p
            .registers
            .iter()
            .map(|r| {
                let key = tag_key(&d.id, &r.id);
                let tv = live.get(&key);
                let raw = live.last_raw(&key).map(<[u16]>::to_vec);
                let dt = r.data_type();
                let decoded = match (&raw, dt) {
                    (Some(words), Some(dt)) => codec::decode(dt, r.word_order, words).ok().map(|v| v.display()),
                    _ => None,
                };
                let orders = match (&raw, dt) {
                    (Some(words), Some(dt)) if r.type_name.needs_word_order() => codec::decode_all_orders(dt, words)
                        .into_iter()
                        .map(|(o, res)| OrderValue {
                            order: o.as_str(),
                            is_profile: r.word_order == Some(o),
                            value: res.as_ref().ok().map(|v| v.display()),
                            error: res.err().map(|e| e.to_string()),
                        })
                        .collect(),
                    _ => Vec::new(),
                };
                let f = r.table.read_function();
                InspectRow {
                    tag_id: r.id.clone(),
                    name: r.name.clone(),
                    table: r.table.as_str(),
                    doc_address: r.doc_label(),
                    pdu_offset: r.address,
                    function: f.code(),
                    function_name: f.name(),
                    type_name: r.type_name,
                    word_order: r.word_order.map(|o| o.as_str()),
                    width: r.width(),
                    unit: r.unit.clone(),
                    raw_hex: raw.as_deref().map(export::raw_hex),
                    raw,
                    decoded,
                    value: tv.and_then(|t| t.value),
                    orders,
                    quality: tv.map(|t| t.quality),
                    exception: tv.and_then(|t| t.exception),
                    exception_name: tv.and_then(|t| t.exception).map(|c| ExceptionCode(c).name()),
                    error: tv.and_then(|t| t.error.clone()),
                    value_ts_ms: tv.and_then(|t| t.value_ts_ms),
                }
            })
            .collect();
        drop(live);
        let frames = lock(&self.shared.frames).of(&d.link_id, d.unit_id);
        Ok(DeviceInspection {
            device: view,
            rows,
            frames,
        })
    }

    // ---- alarms ----

    pub fn alarm_add(&self, def: AlarmDef) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        self.find_device(&def.device_id)?;
        let now = self.shared.now();
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).add(def, now).map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarm_remove(&self, id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).remove(id).map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarm_ack(&self, id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).ack(id, now).map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarm_shelve(&self, id: &str, duration_ms: u64) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        let until = now.saturating_add(i64::try_from(duration_ms).unwrap_or(i64::MAX));
        lock(&self.shared.alarms)
            .shelve(id, until, now)
            .map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarm_unshelve(&self, id: &str) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).unshelve(id, now).map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarm_set_out_of_service(&self, id: &str, oos: bool) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        lock(&self.shared.alarms)
            .set_out_of_service(id, oos, now)
            .map_err(SessionError::Alarm)
    }

    pub fn alarms(&self) -> AlarmSnapshot {
        let now = self.shared.now();
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).snapshot(now)
    }

    pub fn alarm_defs(&self) -> Vec<AlarmDef> {
        lock(&self.shared.alarms).defs()
    }

    /// Samples applied to the live store so far (diagnostics and tests).
    pub fn applied_samples(&self) -> u64 {
        lock(&self.shared.live).applied()
    }

    /// Stop every worker, flush the historian and end the hub thread.
    pub fn shutdown(&self) {
        {
            let mut links = lock(&self.shared.links);
            for e in links.values_mut() {
                self.shared.stop_worker(e);
                if let Some(t) = e.transport.take() {
                    lock(&t).close();
                }
                e.state = LinkState::Disconnected;
            }
        }
        self.shared.stop.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        if let Some(h) = lock(&self.hub).take() {
            let _ = h.join();
        }
        self.shared.flush_log();
    }
}

impl Drop for Session {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.shutdown();
    }
}

/// P10: random operation sequences.
#[test]
fn state_machine_never_sends_without_confirmation_and_never_twice() {
    let mut total_sends = 0u64;
    check("command_state_machine", 500, |r| {
        let mut w = World::new();
        let audit = MemoryAudit::new();
        let mut svc = service(&w, &audit);
        let targets = [
            target("sim-vfd.json", &sim_link("sim"), 2),
            target("sim-temp-controller.json", &sim_link("sim"), 3),
            target("sim-vfd.json", &rtu_link("bus1"), 2),
        ];
        let roles = [Role::Viewer, Role::Operator, Role::Commissioner];
        // Model: the preview id that is currently confirmed and not yet executed.
        let mut confirmed: Option<u64> = None;
        let mut previewed: Option<u64> = None;
        let mut expected_sends = 0u64;
        for _ in 0..r.range_u64(5, 40) {
            let before = w.write_frames().len();
            // 60 %: the legal next step (so the send path is exercised); 40 %: anything.
            let op = if r.chance(600) {
                match svc.state() {
                    CommandState::Idle | CommandState::Done | CommandState::Failed if svc.armed_device().is_none() => 0,
                    CommandState::Armed | CommandState::Done | CommandState::Failed => 2,
                    CommandState::Previewed => 4,
                    _ => 5,
                }
            } else {
                r.below(9)
            };
            let good_role = op == 0 && r.chance(700);
            match op {
                0 => {
                    let t = if good_role {
                        targets[r.below(2) as usize].clone()
                    } else {
                        r.pick(&targets).unwrap().clone()
                    };
                    let role = if good_role {
                        Role::Commissioner
                    } else {
                        *r.pick(&roles).unwrap()
                    };
                    let ok = svc.arm(t, Operator { user: "u".into(), role }).is_ok();
                    if ok || svc.armed_device().is_none() {
                        confirmed = None;
                        previewed = None;
                    }
                }
                1 => {
                    svc.disarm(DisarmReason::Operator);
                    confirmed = None;
                    previewed = None;
                }
                2 | 3 => {
                    let pick = match svc.armed_unit() {
                        Some(2) if r.chance(700) => {
                            if r.chance(700) {
                                0
                            } else {
                                2
                            }
                        }
                        Some(3) if r.chance(700) => 1,
                        _ => r.below(4),
                    };
                    let (reg, v) = match pick.min(3) {
                        0 => ("freq_setpoint", r.range_u64(0, 6000) as f64 / 100.0),
                        1 => ("sp", r.range_u64(0, 1300) as f64 / 10.0),
                        2 => ("control_word", r.range_u64(0, 5) as f64),
                        _ => ("ramp_time", r.unit_f64() * 70.0),
                    };
                    match svc.preview(&mut w.link(), set(reg, v)) {
                        Ok(p) => {
                            previewed = Some(p.id);
                            assert!(confirmed.is_none());
                        }
                        Err(CommandError::WrongState { .. }) => {}
                        Err(_) => {
                            if svc.state() == CommandState::Idle {
                                previewed = None;
                                confirmed = None;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }

// Trends (dashboard-ui Req 4): uPlot, null gaps with hatched bands and reasons, alarm-limit bands,
// drag-zoom + reset, ≤ 4 Hz refresh. Live ranges come from the store; long ranges from the historian
// with min-max decimation in Rust.
import uPlot from "uplot";
import "uplot/dist/uPlot.min.css";
import { api, errorText } from "../api.ts";
import { clear, h } from "../dom.ts";
import { fmtLocalTime, fmtNumber, fmtUtc } from "../format.ts";
import { lang, t, tx } from "../i18n.ts";
import { loadProfiles, profileOf } from "../profiles.ts";
import { align, bufferToSeries, NO_DATA, type Series } from "../series.ts";
import { store } from "../store.ts";
import { cssVar, onThemeChange } from "../theme.ts";
import type { AlarmView, DeviceView, Gap, Register } from "../types.ts";
import { statusLine, type View } from "./view.ts";

interface TagRef {
  key: string;
  device: DeviceView;
  reg: Register;
}

type RangeId = "5m" | "15m" | "30m" | "1h" | "8h" | "session";
const LIVE: Record<string, number> = { "5m": 5 * 60_000, "15m": 15 * 60_000, "30m": 30 * 60_000 };
const HIST: Record<string, number> = { "1h": 3_600_000, "8h": 8 * 3_600_000 };
const MAX_TAGS = 6;
const DASHES: number[][] = [[], [10, 5], [2, 4], [14, 4, 3, 4], [6, 3], [1, 3]];
const REFRESH_MS = 250;

export function gapLabel(g: Gap): string {
  return g.reason === NO_DATA ? t("trend.no_data") : t("trend.no_data_reason", { reason: g.reason });
}

function numericRegisters(d: DeviceView): Register[] {
  return (profileOf(d)?.registers ?? []).filter((r) => r.type !== "string" && r.type !== "bool");
}

function hatch(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, color: string): CanvasPattern | string {
  const c = document.createElement("canvas");
  c.width = 10;
  c.height = 10;
  const g = c.getContext("2d");
  if (!g) return color;
  g.strokeStyle = color;
  g.globalAlpha = 0.45;
  g.lineWidth = 2;
  g.beginPath();
  g.moveTo(0, 10);
  g.lineTo(10, 0);
  g.stroke();
  return ctx.createPattern(c, "repeat") ?? color;
}

export function trendsView(params: { device?: string } = {}): View {
  const selected = new Set<string>();
  let range: RangeId = "5m";
  let charts: { plot: uPlot; tags: TagRef[]; series: Series[]; box: HTMLElement }[] = [];
  let zoomed = false;
  let pending = false;
  let lastDraw = 0;
  const status = statusLine();
  const picker = h("fieldset", { class: "card tag-picker" });
  const chartsBox = h("div", { class: "charts" });
  const note = h("p", { class: "muted small", role: "note" });
  const gapsList = h("ul", { class: "gap-list", "aria-label": t("trend.gaps") });

  const rangeBox = h("div", { class: "segmented", role: "group", "aria-label": t("trend.range") });
  const ranges: RangeId[] = ["5m", "15m", "30m", "1h", "8h", "session"];
  for (const r of ranges) {
    const b = h("button", { type: "button", "aria-pressed": String(r === range), "data-range": r }, t(`trend.range.${r}`));
    b.addEventListener("click", () => {
      range = r;
      zoomed = false;
      for (const x of rangeBox.querySelectorAll("button")) x.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(x.dataset.range === r));
      void rebuild();
    });
    rangeBox.append(b);
  }
  const resetBtn = h("button", { type: "button" }, t("trend.reset_zoom"));
  resetBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    zoomed = false;
    void draw(true);
  });
  const reloadBtn = h("button", { type: "button" }, t("trend.reload"));
  reloadBtn.addEventListener("click", () => void draw(true));

  function tagRefs(): TagRef[] {
    const out: TagRef[] = [];
    for (const { device } of store.devices()) {
      for (const reg of numericRegisters(device)) {
        const key = `${device.id}/${reg.id}`;
        if (selected.has(key)) out.push({ key, device, reg });
      }
    }
    return out;
  }

  function renderPicker() {
    clear(picker);
    picker.append(h("legend", null, t("trend.pick", { n: MAX_TAGS })));
    for (const { device } of store.devices()) {
      const regs = numericRegisters(device);
      if (!regs.length) continue;
      const group = h("div", { class: "pick-group" }, h("p", { class: "pick-device" }, device.name));
      for (const reg of regs) {
        const key = `${device.id}/${reg.id}`;
        const cb = h("input", { type: "checkbox", value: key, checked: selected.has(key) });
        cb.addEventListener("change", () => {
          if (cb.checked) {
            if (selected.size >= MAX_TAGS) {
              cb.checked = false;
              status.set(t("trend.too_many", { n: MAX_TAGS }), "error");
              return;
            }
            selected.add(key);
          } else selected.delete(key);
          void rebuild();
        });
        group.append(h("label", { class: "check" }, cb, ` ${tx(reg.name)}${reg.unit ? ` (${reg.unit})` : ""}`));
      }
      picker.append(group);
    }
  }

  function bounds(): { from: number; to: number } {
    const now = Date.now();
    if (range in LIVE) return { from: now - (LIVE[range] ?? 300_000), to: now };
    if (range in HIST) return { from: now - (HIST[range] ?? 3_600_000), to: now };
    return { from: 0, to: now };
  }

  async function seriesFor(tags: TagRef[], width: number): Promise<{ series: Series[]; decimated: boolean }> {
    const { from, to } = bounds();
    if (range in LIVE) {
      return {

        decimated: false,
      };
    }
    const res = await Promise.all(
      tags.map((tg) => api.trend({ device_id: tg.device.id, tag_id: tg.reg.id, from_ms: from, to_ms: to, buckets: Math.max(50, Math.floor(width)) })),
    );

      series: res.map((r) => ({ t: r.t, v: r.v, gaps: r.gaps })),
      decimated: res.some((r) => r.decimated),
    };
  }

  function groups(tags: TagRef[]): TagRef[][] {
    // At most two units (two y-axes) per chart.
    const units = [...new Set(tags.map((tg) => tg.reg.unit ?? ""))];
    const out: TagRef[][] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < units.length; i += 2) {
      const us = units.slice(i, i + 2);
      out.push(tags.filter((tg) => us.includes(tg.reg.unit ?? "")));
    }

  }

  function makePlot(box: HTMLElement, tags: TagRef[], getSeries: () => Series[], getAlarms: () => AlarmView[]): uPlot {
    const L = lang();
    const text = cssVar("--text") || "#1F1F1F";
    const muted = cssVar("--text-muted") || "#4D4D4D";
    const grid = cssVar("--grid") || "#C4C4C4";
    const bad = cssVar("--quality-bad") || "#AA3377";
    const palette = [cssVar("--series-1"), cssVar("--series-2"), cssVar("--series-3"), cssVar("--series-4"), cssVar("--series-5"), cssVar("--series-6")];
    const units = [...new Set(tags.map((tg) => tg.reg.unit ?? ""))];

      height: 260,

          points: { show: false },

      axes: [
        { stroke: muted, grid: { stroke: grid, width: 1 }, ticks: { stroke: grid } },

          scale: u || "_",
          side: i === 0 ? 3 : 1,
          label: u || t("trend.value"),
          stroke: muted,
          grid: { show: i === 0, stroke: grid, width: 1 },
          ticks: { stroke: grid },
          values: (_u: uPlot, vals: number[]) => vals.map((v) => fmtNumber(v, L)),

        drawClear: [
          (u) => {
            const ctx = u.ctx;
            const { left, top, width, height } = u.bbox;
            ctx.save();
            ctx.beginPath();
            ctx.rect(left, top, width, height);
            ctx.clip();
            // Alarm-limit bands.
            for (const a of getAlarms()) {
              const tg = tags.find((x) => x.device.id === a.device_id && x.reg.id === a.tag_id);
              if (!tg || a.limit === null) continue;
              const y = u.valToPos(a.limit, tg.reg.unit || "_", true);
              if (!Number.isFinite(y)) continue;
              const high = a.kind === "HI" || a.kind === "HI_HI";
              ctx.globalAlpha = 0.12;
              ctx.fillStyle = prioColor(a.priority);
              if (high) ctx.fillRect(left, top, width, Math.max(0, y - top));

              ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
              ctx.strokeStyle = prioColor(a.priority);
              ctx.setLineDash([6, 4]);
              ctx.lineWidth = 1.5;
              ctx.beginPath();

              ctx.lineTo(left + width, y);
              ctx.stroke();

                const x1 = Math.min(left + width, u.valToPos(g.to_ms, "x", true));

              tooltip.textContent = "";
              return;
            }
            const x = u.data[0][idx];
            if (x === undefined) return;
            const lines = [`${fmtLocalTime(x, lang())} · UTC ${fmtUtc(x)}`];
            getSeries().forEach((s, i) => {
              const v = u.data[i + 1]?.[idx];
              const gap = s.gaps.find((g) => x >= g.from_ms && x <= g.to_ms);
              const name = tags[i] ? tx(tags[i].reg.name) : "";

          },

      renderGapList();
    } catch (e) {
      status.set(errorText(e), "error");
    }
  }

    for (const c of charts) c.plot.destroy();
    charts = [];
    clear(chartsBox);
    const tags = tagRefs();
    if (!tags.length) {
      chartsBox.append(h("p", { class: "muted" }, t("trend.empty")));

      return;
    }
    for (const g of groups(tags)) {
      const box = h("figure", { class: "card chart", "aria-label": t("trend.chart_label", { tags: g.map((x) => tx(x.reg.name)).join(", ") }) });

      const entry: { plot: uPlot; tags: TagRef[]; series: Series[]; box: HTMLElement } = {
        plot: null as unknown as uPlot,
        tags: g,
        series: [],
        box,
      };
      entry.plot = makePlot(
        box,
        g,
        () => entry.series,
        () => store.alarms.alarms.filter((a) => a.class === "process" && g.some((x) => x.device.id === a.device_id && x.reg.id === a.tag_id)),
      );
      charts.push(entry);
    }
    await draw(true);
  }

    if (c.links) {
      const before = picker.querySelectorAll("input").length;
      const count = store.devices().reduce((n, d) => n + numericRegisters(d.device).length, 0);
      if (before !== count) renderPicker();

  });

    for (const c of charts) c.plot.setSize({ width: Math.max(280, c.box.clientWidth - 8), height: 260 });
  });
  ro.observe(chartsBox);
  let destroyed = false;
  onThemeChange(() => {
    if (!destroyed) void rebuild();
  });

  const el = h(
    "div",
    { class: "view trends" },
    h("header", { class: "view-head" }, h("h2", null, t("nav.trends")), h("div", { class: "actions" }, rangeBox, resetBtn, reloadBtn)),
    h("p", { class: "muted small" }, t("trend.help")),
    status.el,
    h("div", { class: "trend-layout" }, picker, h("div", { class: "trend-main" }, chartsBox, note, h("h3", null, t("trend.gaps")), gapsList)),
  );

  void loadProfiles().then(() => {
    const devs = store.devices();
    const first = params.device ? devs.find((d) => d.device.id === params.device) : devs[0];
    if (first) for (const r of numericRegisters(first.device).slice(0, 2)) selected.add(`${first.device.id}/${r.id}`);
    renderPicker();
    void rebuild();
  });
  return {
    el,
    destroy() {
      destroyed = true;
      unsub();
      ro.disconnect();
      for (const c of charts) c.plot.destroy();
    },
  };
}

              `${tag ? `${tag.device.name}: ${tx(tag.reg.name)} — ` : ""}${gapLabel(g)} · ${fmtLocalTime(g.from_ms, L)}–${fmtLocalTime(g.to_ms, L)}`,
            ),
          );
        }
      }),
    );
    if (n === 0) gapsList.append(h("li", { class: "muted" }, t("trend.gaps.none")));
  }

  async function draw(force = false) {
    if (!charts.length) return;
    const now = Date.now();
    if (!force && now - lastDraw < REFRESH_MS) {
      if (!pending) {
        pending = true;
        window.setTimeout(() => {
          pending = false;
          void draw(true);
        }, REFRESH_MS);
      }
      return;
    }
    lastDraw = now;
    const started = performance.now();
    let anyDecimated = false;
    try {
      for (const c of charts) {
        const { series, decimated } = await seriesFor(c.tags, c.box.clientWidth);
        anyDecimated ||= decimated;
        c.series = series;
        const { x, ys } = align(series);
        c.plot.setData([x, ...ys] as uPlot.AlignedData, false);
        if (!zoomed) {
          const { from, to } = bounds();
          const min = range === "session" ? (x[0] ?? from) : from;
          c.plot.setScale("x", { min, max: to });
        }
      }
      note.textContent = `${anyDecimated ? t("trend.decimated") : range in LIVE ? t("trend.raw_live") : t("trend.raw")} · ${t("trend.render_ms", { ms: fmtNumber(performance.now() - started, lang(), 1) })}`;
      renderGapList();
    } catch (e) {
      status.set(errorText(e), "error");
    }
  }

  async function rebuild() {
    for (const c of charts) c.plot.destroy();
    charts = [];
    clear(chartsBox);
    const tags = tagRefs();
    if (!tags.length) {
      chartsBox.append(h("p", { class: "muted" }, t("trend.empty")));
      renderGapList();
      return;
    }
    for (const g of groups(tags)) {
      const box = h("figure", { class: "card chart", "aria-label": t("trend.chart_label", { tags: g.map((x) => tx(x.reg.name)).join(", ") }) });
      chartsBox.append(box);
      const entry: { plot: uPlot; tags: TagRef[]; series: Series[]; box: HTMLElement } = {
        plot: null as unknown as uPlot,
        tags: g,
        series: [],
        box,
      };
      entry.plot = makePlot(
        box,
        g,
        () => entry.series,
        () => store.alarms.alarms.filter((a) => a.class === "process" && g.some((x) => x.device.id === a.device_id && x.reg.id === a.tag_id)),
      );
      charts.push(entry);
    }
    await draw(true);
  }

  const unsub = store.subscribe((c) => {
    if (c.links) {
      const before = picker.querySelectorAll("input").length;
      const count = store.devices().reduce((n, d) => n + numericRegisters(d.device).length, 0);
      if (before !== count) renderPicker();
    }
    if (c.points && range in LIVE) void draw();
  });
  const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => {
    for (const c of charts) c.plot.setSize({ width: Math.max(280, c.box.clientWidth - 8), height: 260 });
  });
  ro.observe(chartsBox);
  let destroyed = false;
  onThemeChange(() => {
    if (!destroyed) void rebuild();
  });

  const el = h(
    "div",
    { class: "view trends" },
    h("header", { class: "view-head" }, h("h2", null, t("nav.trends")), h("div", { class: "actions" }, rangeBox, resetBtn, reloadBtn)),
    h("p", { class: "muted small" }, t("trend.help")),
    status.el,
    h("div", { class: "trend-layout" }, picker, h("div", { class: "trend-main" }, chartsBox, note, h("h3", null, t("trend.gaps")), gapsList)),
  );

  void loadProfiles().then(() => {
    const devs = store.devices();
    const first = params.device ? devs.find((d) => d.device.id === params.device) : devs[0];
    if (first) for (const r of numericRegisters(first.device).slice(0, 2)) selected.add(`${first.device.id}/${r.id}`);
    renderPicker();
    void rebuild();
  });
  return {
    el,
    destroy() {
      destroyed = true;
      unsub();
      ro.disconnect();
      for (const c of charts) c.plot.destroy();
    },
  };
}

// Store buffers → uPlot data. Gaps are gaps: non-GOOD points are `null` (uPlot breaks the line),
// holes longer than the stale threshold get a `null` too, and every gap is returned with its reason.
// `undefined` is only used for alignment between series (uPlot spans it; it never stands for lost data).
import type { Gap } from "./types.ts";
import type { TrendBuffer } from "./store.ts";

export const NO_DATA = "NO_DATA";

export interface Series {
  t: number[];
  v: (number | null)[];
  gaps: Gap[];
}

export function bufferToSeries(b: TrendBuffer | undefined, from: number, to: number, staleMs: number): Series {
  const out: Series = { t: [], v: [], gaps: [] };
  if (!b) return out;
  let lastGood: number | null = null;
  let open: Gap | null = null;
  for (let i = 0; i < b.t.length; i++) {
    const t = b.t[i] ?? 0;
    if (t < from || t > to) continue;
    const q = b.q[i];
    const v = b.v[i];
    const good = q === "GOOD" && v !== null && v !== undefined && Number.isFinite(v);
    if (good) {
      if (open) {
        open.to_ms = t;
        open = null;
      } else if (lastGood !== null && t - lastGood > staleMs) {
        out.t.push(lastGood + (t - lastGood) / 2);
        out.v.push(null);
        out.gaps.push({ from_ms: lastGood, to_ms: t, reason: NO_DATA });
      }
      out.t.push(t);
      out.v.push(v);
      lastGood = t;
    } else {
      if (!open) {
        open = { from_ms: lastGood ?? t, to_ms: t, reason: q === "EXCEPTION" ? "EXCEPTION" : (q ?? NO_DATA) };
        out.gaps.push(open);
        out.t.push(t);
        out.v.push(null);
      } else {
        open.to_ms = t;
      }
      lastGood = null;
    }
  }
  // Nothing new for longer than the stale threshold: the tail is a gap, not a flat line.
  if (open) {
    open.to_ms = Math.max(open.to_ms, to);
  } else if (lastGood !== null && to - lastGood > staleMs) {
    out.gaps.push({ from_ms: lastGood, to_ms: to, reason: NO_DATA });
  }
  return out;
}

/** Merge several series onto one x array for uPlot. Own nulls stay null; other series' x get undefined. */
export function align(series: Series[]): { x: number[]; ys: (number | null | undefined)[][] } {
  const xs = [...new Set(series.flatMap((s) => s.t))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const index = new Map(xs.map((x, i) => [x, i]));
  const ys = series.map((s) => {
    const y: (number | null | undefined)[] = new Array(xs.length).fill(undefined);
    s.t.forEach((t, i) => {
      const at = index.get(t);
      if (at === undefined) return;
      const v = s.v[i];
      // A null always wins over a value at the same instant: never hide a gap.
      if (v === null || y[at] === undefined) y[at] = v ?? null;
    });
    return y;
  });
  return { x: xs, ys };
}

// U1/U2: store buffers → uPlot series. Run with `node --test` (type stripping).
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { align, bufferToSeries, NO_DATA } from "./series.ts";
import type { TrendBuffer } from "./store.ts";
import type { QualityCode } from "./types.ts";

function buf(points: [number, number | null, QualityCode][]): TrendBuffer {
  return { t: points.map((p) => p[0]), v: points.map((p) => p[1]), q: points.map((p) => p[2]) };
}

test("U1 non-GOOD points become null, never a number", () => {
  const s = bufferToSeries(
    buf([
      [0, 1, "GOOD"],
      [1000, 2, "GOOD"],
      [2000, 999, "TIMEOUT"],
      [3000, 999, "TIMEOUT"],
      [4000, 3, "GOOD"],
    ]),
    0,
    4000,
    5000,
  );
  assert.deepEqual(s.v, [1, 2, null, 3]);
  assert.deepEqual(s.gaps, [{ from_ms: 1000, to_ms: 4000, reason: "TIMEOUT" }]);
});

test("U1 random buffers: every value comes from a GOOD point", () => {
  let seed = 7;
  const rnd = () => ((seed = (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2 ** 31) / 2 ** 31);
  const qs: QualityCode[] = ["GOOD", "GOOD", "GOOD", "TIMEOUT", "STALE", "CRC_ERROR", "EXCEPTION", "DISCONNECTED"];
  for (let c = 0; c < 200; c++) {
    let t = 0;
    const pts: [number, number | null, QualityCode][] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
      t += 1 + Math.floor(rnd() * 3000);
      pts.push([t, Math.round(rnd() * 100), qs[Math.floor(rnd() * qs.length)] ?? "GOOD"]);
    }
    const b = buf(pts);
    const s = bufferToSeries(b, 0, t, 2000);
    s.t.forEach((x, i) => {
      const v = s.v[i];
      if (v === null || v === undefined) return;
      const j = b.t.indexOf(x);
      assert.ok(j >= 0 && b.q[j] === "GOOD" && b.v[j] === v, `value ${v} at ${x} is not GOOD`);
    });
    // U2: two consecutive drawn values never straddle a bad point or a hole longer than the threshold.
    for (let i = 1; i < s.t.length; i++) {
      const [a, bb] = [s.t[i - 1] ?? 0, s.t[i] ?? 0];
      if (s.v[i - 1] === null || s.v[i] === null) continue;
      assert.ok(bb - a <= 2000, `hole ${a}..${bb} drawn over`);
      for (let j = 0; j < b.t.length; j++) {
        const x = b.t[j] ?? 0;
        if (x > a && x < bb) assert.equal(b.q[j], "GOOD");
      }
    }
  }
});

test("U2 holes and a silent tail are NO_DATA gaps", () => {
  const s = bufferToSeries(
    buf([
      [0, 1, "GOOD"],
      [10_000, 2, "GOOD"],
    ]),
    0,
    30_000,
    3000,
  );
  assert.deepEqual(s.v, [1, null, 2]);
  assert.equal(s.gaps.length, 2);
  assert.equal(s.gaps[0]?.reason, NO_DATA);
  assert.deepEqual([s.gaps[1]?.from_ms, s.gaps[1]?.to_ms], [10_000, 30_000]);
});

test("align keeps own nulls and uses undefined only for alignment", () => {
  const a = { t: [1, 2, 3], v: [1, null, 3], gaps: [] };
  const b = { t: [2, 4], v: [5, 6], gaps: [] };
  const { x, ys } = align([a, b]);
  assert.deepEqual(x, [1, 2, 3, 4]);
  assert.deepEqual(ys[0], [1, null, 3, undefined]);
  assert.deepEqual(ys[1], [undefined, 5, undefined, 6]);
});

// Live state in the webview. Pure (no DOM) so it can be unit-tested with node --test.
import type {
  AlarmSnapshot,
  AlarmView,
  DeviceView,
  LinkView,
  LiveFrame,
  LiveSnapshot,
  QualityCode,
  TagView,
} from "./types.ts";

export const BUFFER_MS = 30 * 60_000;
export const MAX_POINTS_PER_TAG = 7_200;

export interface TrendBuffer {
  t: number[];
  v: (number | null)[];
  q: QualityCode[];
}

export interface Change {
  tags: Set<string>;
  links: boolean;
  alarms: boolean;
  points: boolean;
}

export const EMPTY_ALARMS: AlarmSnapshot = {
  alarms: [],
  summary: {
    counts: [0, 0, 0],
    unacked: 0,
    oldest_unacked: null,
    oldest_unacked_ms: null,
    activations_10min: 0,
    flood: false,
    comm_active: 0,
  },
};

export class Store {
  tags = new Map<string, TagView>();
  links: LinkView[] = [];
  alarms: AlarmSnapshot = EMPTY_ALARMS;
  historianError: string | null = null;
  droppedTotal = 0;
  lastFrameMs = 0;
  buffers = new Map<string, TrendBuffer>();
  private listeners = new Set<(c: Change) => void>();

  subscribe(f: (c: Change) => void): () => void {
    this.listeners.add(f);
    return () => this.listeners.delete(f);
  }

  private emit(c: Change): void {
    for (const f of this.listeners) f(c);
  }

  applySnapshot(s: LiveSnapshot): void {
    this.tags.clear();
    for (const tag of s.tags) this.tags.set(tag.key, tag);
    this.links = s.links;
    this.alarms = s.alarms;
    this.historianError = s.historian_error;
    this.emit({ tags: new Set(this.tags.keys()), links: true, alarms: true, points: false });
  }

  applyFrame(f: LiveFrame): void {
    this.lastFrameMs = f.ts_ms;
    const changed = new Set<string>();
    for (const tag of f.tags) {
      this.tags.set(tag.key, tag);
      changed.add(tag.key);
    }
    for (const p of f.points) {
      let b = this.buffers.get(p.k);
      if (!b) {
        b = { t: [], v: [], q: [] };
        this.buffers.set(p.k, b);
      }
      // Points arrive in publish order; keep the buffer sorted even if a late one slips in.
      const last = b.t[b.t.length - 1];
      if (last !== undefined && p.t < last) {
        let i = b.t.length;
        while (i > 0 && (b.t[i - 1] ?? 0) > p.t) i--;
        b.t.splice(i, 0, p.t);
        b.v.splice(i, 0, p.q === "GOOD" ? p.v : null);
        b.q.splice(i, 0, p.q);
      } else {
        b.t.push(p.t);
        b.v.push(p.q === "GOOD" ? p.v : null);
        b.q.push(p.q);
      }
    }
    this.trim(f.ts_ms);
    this.droppedTotal += f.dropped;
    if (f.links) this.links = f.links;
    if (f.alarms) this.alarms = f.alarms;
    this.historianError = f.historian_error;
    this.emit({ tags: changed, links: f.links !== null, alarms: f.alarms !== null, points: f.points.length > 0 });
  }

  private trim(now: number): void {
    const oldest = now - BUFFER_MS;
    for (const b of this.buffers.values()) {
      let cut = 0;
      while (cut < b.t.length && (b.t[cut] ?? 0) < oldest) cut++;
      cut = Math.max(cut, b.t.length - MAX_POINTS_PER_TAG);
      if (cut > 0) {
        b.t.splice(0, cut);
        b.v.splice(0, cut);
        b.q.splice(0, cut);
      }
    }
  }

  devices(): { device: DeviceView; link: LinkView }[] {
    return this.links.flatMap((link) => link.devices.map((device) => ({ device, link })));
  }

  device(id: string): { device: DeviceView; link: LinkView } | undefined {
    return this.devices().find((d) => d.device.id === id);
  }

  tagsOf(deviceId: string): TagView[] {
    return [...this.tags.values()].filter((t) => t.device_id === deviceId);
  }

  alarmsOfTag(deviceId: string, tagId: string): AlarmView[] {
    return this.alarms.alarms.filter((a) => a.class === "process" && a.device_id === deviceId && a.tag_id === tagId);
  }

  commAlarm(deviceId: string): AlarmView | undefined {
    return this.alarms.alarms.find((a) => a.class === "comm" && a.device_id === deviceId);
  }
}

export const store = new Store();

</content>
</file>

    flood: false,
    comm_active: 0,
  },
};

export class Store {
  tags = new Map<string, TagView>();
  links: LinkView[] = [];
  alarms: AlarmSnapshot = EMPTY_ALARMS;
  historianError: string | null = null;
  droppedTotal = 0;
  lastFrameMs = 0;
  buffers = new Map<string, TrendBuffer>();
  private listeners = new Set<(c: Change) => void>();

  subscribe(f: (c: Change) => void): () => void {
    this.listeners.add(f);
    return () => this.listeners.delete(f);
  }

  private emit(c: Change): void {
    for (const f of this.listeners) f(c);
  }

  applySnapshot(s: LiveSnapshot): void {
    this.tags.clear();
    for (const tag of s.tags) this.tags.set(tag.key, tag);
    this.links = s.links;
    this.alarms = s.alarms;
    this.historianError = s.historian_error;
    this.emit({ tags: new Set(this.tags.keys()), links: true, alarms: true, points: false });
  }

  applyFrame(f: LiveFrame): void {
    this.lastFrameMs = f.ts_ms;
    const changed = new Set<string>();
    for (const tag of f.tags) {
      this.tags.set(tag.key, tag);
      changed.add(tag.key);
    }
    for (const p of f.points) {
      let b = this.buffers.get(p.k);
      if (!b) {
        b = { t: [], v: [], q: [] };
        this.buffers.set(p.k, b);
      }
      // Points arrive in publish order; keep the buffer sorted even if a late one slips in.
      const last = b.t[b.t.length - 1];
      if (last !== undefined && p.t < last) {
        let i = b.t.length;
        while (i > 0 && (b.t[i - 1] ?? 0) > p.t) i--;
        b.t.splice(i, 0, p.t);
        b.v.splice(i, 0, p.q === "GOOD" ? p.v : null);
        b.q.splice(i, 0, p.q);
      } else {
        b.t.push(p.t);
        b.v.push(p.q === "GOOD" ? p.v : null);
        b.q.push(p.q);
      }
    }
    this.trim(f.ts_ms);
    this.droppedTotal += f.dropped;
    if (f.links) this.links = f.links;
    if (f.alarms) this.alarms = f.alarms;
    this.historianError = f.historian_error;
    this.emit({ tags: changed, links: f.links !== null, alarms: f.alarms !== null, points: f.points.length > 0 });
  }

  private trim(now: number): void {
    const oldest = now - BUFFER_MS;
    for (const b of this.buffers.values()) {
      let cut = 0;
      while (cut < b.t.length && (b.t[cut] ?? 0) < oldest) cut++;
      cut = Math.max(cut, b.t.length - MAX_POINTS_PER_TAG);
      if (cut > 0) {
        b.t.splice(0, cut);
        b.v.splice(0, cut);
        b.q.splice(0, cut);
      }
    }
  }

  devices(): { device: DeviceView; link: LinkView }[] {
    return this.links.flatMap((link) => link.devices.map((device) => ({ device, link })));
  }

  device(id: string): { device: DeviceView; link: LinkView } | undefined {
    return this.devices().find((d) => d.device.id === id);
  }

  tagsOf(deviceId: string): TagView[] {
    return [...this.tags.values()].filter((t) => t.device_id === deviceId);
  }

  alarmsOfTag(deviceId: string, tagId: string): AlarmView[] {
    return this.alarms.alarms.filter((a) => a.class === "process" && a.device_id === deviceId && a.tag_id === tagId);
  }

  commAlarm(deviceId: string): AlarmView | undefined {
    return this.alarms.alarms.find((a) => a.class === "comm" && a.device_id === deviceId);
  }
}

export const store = new Store();

</content>
</file>

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct ExportResult {
    saved: bool,
    path: Option<String>,
    bytes: usize,
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn export_session(app: AppHandle, state: State<'_, AppState>, format: ExportFormat) -> R<ExportResult> {
    let s = Arc::clone(&state.session);
    let name = format!("buslink-{}.{}", s.session_id(), format.extension());
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || -> R<ExportResult> {
        let bytes = s.export(format).map_err(err)?;
        #[cfg(feature = "e2e")]
        if let Ok(dir) = std::env::var("BUSLINK_E2E_EXPORT_DIR") {
            let path = std::path::Path::new(&dir).join(&name);
            std::fs::write(&path, &bytes).map_err(|e| format!("could not write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
            return Ok(ExportResult {
                saved: true,
                path: Some(path.display().to_string()),
                bytes: bytes.len(),
            });
        }
        let (label, ext) = match format {
            ExportFormat::Csv => ("CSV", "csv"),
            ExportFormat::Xlsx => ("Excel workbook", "xlsx"),
            ExportFormat::Json => ("JSON", "json"),
        };
        let picked = app
            .dialog()
            .file()
            .set_file_name(&name)
            .add_filter(label, &[ext])
            .blocking_save_file();
        let Some(fp) = picked else {
            return Ok(ExportResult {
                saved: false,
                path: None,
                bytes: 0,
            });
        };
        let path = fp.into_path().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        std::fs::write(&path, &bytes).map_err(|e| format!("could not write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        Ok(ExportResult {
            saved: true,
            path: Some(path.display().to_string()),
            bytes: bytes.len(),
        })
    })
    .await
    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
}

pub struct TrainingStatus {

}

fn training_of(state: &AppState) -> Option<Arc<Training>> {
    state.training.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn training_status(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> TrainingStatus {
    match training_of(&state) {
        Some(t) => TrainingStatus {
            started: true,
            link_id: TRAINING_LINK_ID,
            units: t.world().lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).units(),
            faults: t.active(),
        },
        None => TrainingStatus {
            started: false,
            link_id: TRAINING_LINK_ID,
            units: Vec::new(),
            faults: Vec::new(),
        },
    }
}

/// Start Training mode: a simulated bus with three devices, alarm presets, polling on.
#[tauri::command]
pub fn training_start(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> R<TrainingStatus> {
    let s = &state.session;
    {
        let mut t = state.training.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if t.is_none() {
            let seed = u64::try_from(state.clock.utc_ms()).unwrap_or(1);
            *t = Some(Arc::new(Training::new(seed, Arc::clone(&state.clock))));
        }
    }
    let existing = s.links().into_iter().find(|l| l.id == TRAINING_LINK_ID);
    match existing {
        Some(l) if l.state == buslink_core::session::LinkState::Polling => {}
        Some(l) => {
            if matches!(
                l.state,
                buslink_core::session::LinkState::Disconnected | buslink_core::session::LinkState::Down
            ) {
                s.reconnect(TRAINING_LINK_ID).map_err(err)?;
            }
            s.start_polling(TRAINING_LINK_ID).map_err(err)?;
        }
        None => {
            let link = Training::link_config();
            s.connect(link.clone(), true).map_err(err)?;
            let mut ids = Vec::new();
            for (unit, profile_id) in TRAINING_DEVICES {
                let Some(p) = s.profiles().into_iter().find(|p| p.profile_id == profile_id) else {
                    return Err(format!("bundled profile {profile_id} missing"));
                };
                let id = s.suggest_device_id(&p.profile_id, unit);
                let mut d = DeviceInstance::from_profile(&id, &format!("{} (simulated)", p.model.get("en")), &link, &p);
                d.unit_id = unit;
                d.response_timeout_ms = Some(300);
                s.add_device(d).map_err(err)?;
                ids.push(id);
            }
            if let [soil, vfd, temp] = ids.as_slice() {
                for a in alarm_presets(soil, vfd, temp) {
                    s.alarm_add(a).map_err(err)?;
                }
            }
            s.start_polling(TRAINING_LINK_ID).map_err(err)?;
        }
    }
    Ok(training_status(state))
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct FaultReq {
    unit: u8,
    fault: TrainingFault,
    seconds: u32,
}

/// Fault injection exists only on the training bus (it acts on the simulator world).
#[tauri::command]
pub fn training_fault(state: State<'_, AppState>, req: FaultReq) -> R<TrainingStatus> {
    let t = training_of(&state).ok_or("Training mode is not started")?;
    t.inject(req.unit, req.fault, u64::from(req.seconds) * 1000)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    Ok(training_status(state))
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn training_clear(state: State<'_, AppState>, unit: u8) -> R<TrainingStatus> {
    let t = training_of(&state).ok_or("Training mode is not started")?;
    t.clear(unit);
    Ok(training_status(state))
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PreToolUse guard for BusLink Studio file writes (stdlib only).

Kiro pipes the hook event as JSON on stdin:
  {"hook_event_name": "PreToolUse", "cwd": "...", "tool_name": "fs_write",
   "tool_input": {"path": "...", "text": "..."}}

Only the lines a write would ADD are inspected. The guard blocks (exit 2,
reason on stderr) when an edit:
  1. adds Modbus write function codes (FC05/06/15/16, FC22/23) or write API
     names (write_single_register, ...) in source code outside
     crates/buslink-core/src/command/**, crates/buslink-sim/** and tests;
  2. adds a write addressed to the broadcast unit ID 0 (anywhere except tests);
  3. adds something that looks like a secret (API key, token, MQTT password,
     private key). Generic `password = "..."` assignments are allowed in
     example/sample files; high-confidence key formats are blocked everywhere.

Parse problems fail open: a warning on stderr and exit 1 (Kiro shows the
warning and the tool still runs). See .kiro/steering/safety.md.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(os.environ.get("BUSLINK_ROOT") or pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2])

WRITE_TOOLS = {"fs_write", "fs_append", "str_replace", "write", "fsWrite", "fsAppend", "strReplace", "create_file"}

CODE_EXT = {".rs", ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".kt", ".kts", ".java", ".html", ".vue", ".svelte"}

# Paths (relative, POSIX) where Modbus write code is allowed to live.
WRITE_CODE_ALLOWED = (
    re.compile(r"^crates/buslink-core/src/command/"),
    re.compile(r"^crates/buslink-sim/"),
)
TEST_PATH = re.compile(
    r"(^|/)tests?/"                       # crates/x/tests/..., src/test/...
    r"|(^|/)tests\.rs$"                   # src/foo/tests.rs
    r"|_tests?\.rs$"                      # codec_test.rs
    r"|\.(test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$"      # ui.test.ts, x.spec.js
    r"|(^|/)src/(test|androidTest)/"      # Android unit/instrumented tests
)
# The hook scripts and their fixtures describe the patterns they detect.
SELF_PATH = re.compile(r"^tools/hooks/")

WRITE_NAME = re.compile(
    r"(?i)\b("
    r"masked?_?write_?registers?"
    r"|read_?write_?multiple_?registers"
    r"|write_?(single_?|multiple_?)?(holding_?)?(registers?|coils?)"
    r"|generate_set_(holdings?|coils?)\w*"          # rmodbus request builders
    r")\b"
)
FC_TOKEN=<redacted>

)
FC_ASSIGN = re.compile(
    r"(?i)\b(function_?code|func_?code|function|func|fn_?code|fc)[\"']?\s*(==|:|=)\s*"
    r"(0x0?5|0x0?6|0x0?f|0x10|0x16|0x17|5|6|15|16|22|23)\b"
)

    ResetFault,
    Mode,
}

    pub value: Option<f64>,

    pub expected: Option<f64>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub timeout_ms: Option<u32>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Apply {
    Immediate,
    AfterReboot,
    Unknown,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct CommSetting {
    pub register: String,
    pub apply: Apply,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub codes: Option<BTreeMap<String, u32>>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct CommConfig {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub unit_id: Option<CommSetting>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub baud: Option<CommSetting>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Profile {
    #[serde(rename = "$schema", default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub schema: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "$comment", default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub comment: Option<String>,
    pub schema_version: u32,
    pub profile_id: String,
    pub profile_version: String,
    pub vendor: Text,
    pub model: Text,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub category: Option<Text>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub firmware: Option<Text>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub description: Option<Text>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub notes: Option<Notes>,
    pub support_level: SupportLevel,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub capabilities: Option<Capabilities>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub simulated_only: bool,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub source: Option<Source>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub evidence: Option<Evidence>,
    pub transport: TransportDefaults,
    pub registers: Vec<Register>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub commands: Option<Vec<Command>>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub comm_config: Option<CommConfig>,
}

impl Profile {
    pub fn register(&self, id: &str) -> Option<&Register> {
        self.registers.iter().find(|r| r.id == id)
    }

    pub fn register_index(&self, id: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.registers.iter().position(|r| r.id == id)
    }

    pub fn command(&self, id: &str) -> Option<&Command> {
        self.commands.as_ref()?.iter().find(|c| c.id == id)
    }

    pub fn capability(&self, f: impl Fn(&Capabilities) -> Option<CapabilityLevel>) -> CapabilityLevel {
        self.capabilities
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(f)
            .unwrap_or(CapabilityLevel::Unsupported)
    }

    /// `profile_id@profile_version`, stored with every sample and export.
    pub fn key(&self) -> String {
        format!("{}@{}", self.profile_id, self.profile_version)
    }
}

<file name="crates/buslink-core/src/clock.rs" language="rust" >
<content>
//! Time sources. Monotonic milliseconds drive deadlines, ages and scheduling;
//! UTC milliseconds are what gets stored and exported.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicI64, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

pub trait Clock: Send + Sync {
    /// Monotonic milliseconds since an arbitrary origin. Never goes backwards.
    fn mono_ms(&self) -> u64;
    /// Wall-clock UTC milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
    fn utc_ms(&self) -> i64;
    /// Wait for `ms` milliseconds. A manual clock advances instead of sleeping.
    fn sleep_ms(&self, ms: u64);
}

/// Real clock for the app and the training simulator.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct SystemClock {
    origin: Instant,
}

impl SystemClock {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { origin: Instant::now() }
    }

    pub fn shared() -> Arc<dyn Clock> {
        Arc::new(Self::new())
    }
}

impl Default for SystemClock {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl Clock for SystemClock {
    fn mono_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        u64::try_from(self.origin.elapsed().as_millis()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)
    }

    fn utc_ms(&self) -> i64 {
        match SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH) {
            Ok(d) => i64::try_from(d.as_millis()).unwrap_or(i64::MAX),
            Err(_) => 0,
        }
    }

    fn sleep_ms(&self, ms: u64) {
        if ms > 0 {
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(ms));
        }
    }
}

/// Deterministic clock for tests: time only moves when told to (or when a
/// component "sleeps" on it).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ManualClock {
    mono: AtomicU64,
    utc_origin: AtomicI64,
}

impl ManualClock {
    /// `utc_origin_ms` is the UTC time that corresponds to monotonic 0.
    pub fn new(utc_origin_ms: i64) -> Self {
        Self {
            mono: AtomicU64::new(0),
            utc_origin: AtomicI64::new(utc_origin_ms),
        }
    }

    pub fn shared(utc_origin_ms: i64) -> Arc<ManualClock> {
        Arc::new(Self::new(utc_origin_ms))
    }

    pub fn advance(&self, ms: u64) {
        self.mono.fetch_add(ms, Ordering::SeqCst);
    }

    /// Move to `mono_ms` if it is in the future; never goes backwards.
    pub fn advance_to(&self, mono_ms: u64) {
        self.mono.fetch_max(mono_ms, Ordering::SeqCst);
    }
}

impl Clock for ManualClock {
    fn mono_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        self.mono.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
    }

    fn utc_ms(&self) -> i64 {
        let mono = i64::try_from(self.mono_ms()).unwrap_or(i64::MAX);
        self.utc_origin.load(Ordering::SeqCst).saturating_add(mono)
    }

    fn sleep_ms(&self, ms: u64) {
        self.advance(ms);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn manual_clock_moves_only_forward() {
        let c = ManualClock::new(1_000);
        assert_eq!(c.mono_ms(), 0);
        assert_eq!(c.utc_ms(), 1_000);
        c.advance(250);
        c.sleep_ms(50);
        assert_eq!(c.mono_ms(), 300);
        c.advance_to(100);
        assert_eq!(c.mono_ms(), 300);
        c.advance_to(400);
        assert_eq!(c.utc_ms(), 1_400);
    }

    #[test]
    fn system_clock_is_monotonic() {
        let c = SystemClock::new();
        let a = c.mono_ms();
        let b = c.mono_ms();
        assert!(b >= a);
        assert!(c.utc_ms() > 1_600_000_000_000);
    }
}

# dashboard-ui: tasks

Depends on app-shell-desktop tasks 1–5. After every UI task: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `node --test src/`, `node scripts/check-i18n.mjs`, `node scripts/check-ui.mjs`. After the alarm task: `cargo test --workspace`. A task is `[x]` only when its checks pass.

- [x] 1. Alarm engine (core)
  - `crates/buslink-core/src/alarm/mod.rs`; session integration (observe, tick, events to historian, snapshot in frames); IPC `alarm_list`, `alarm_add`, `alarm_remove`, `alarm_ack`, `alarm_shelve`, `alarm_unshelve`, `alarm_set_out_of_service`, `alarm_events`.
  - Tests: unit tests for every state transition; properties A1–A6 [300 each].
  - _Requirements: 6.1–6.9_

- [x] 2. UI foundation
  - `api.ts`, `types.ts`, `store.ts`, `dom.ts`, `quality.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `theme.ts`, `styles.css`, `main.ts` router and header (language, theme, nav, alarm banner, live regions).
  - Tests: U1–U5; `scripts/check-i18n.mjs`, `scripts/check-ui.mjs`.
  - _Requirements: 8.1–8.8_

- [x] 3. Connection center
  - `views/connect.ts`.
  - _Requirements: 1.1–1.5_

- [x] 4. Device library
  - `views/library.ts`, `components/badges.ts`.
  - _Requirements: 2.1–2.3_

- [x] 5. Live dashboard
  - `views/dashboard.ts`, `components/tile.ts`; worst-first sort, in-place tile updates, density, pause, export buttons.
  - _Requirements: 3.1–3.5, 9.1, 10.1_

- [x] 6. Trends
  - `views/trends.ts` with uPlot, gap bands, alarm bands, zoom, historian ranges.
  - _Requirements: 4.1–4.7_

- [x] 7. Register inspector
  - `views/inspector.ts`.
  - _Requirements: 5.1, 5.2_

- [x] 8. Alarms and training views
  - `views/alarms.ts`, `views/training.ts`, training alarm presets.
  - _Requirements: 6.7, 6.8, 7.1–7.3_

- [x] 9. Verification
  - `scripts/verify-journey.mjs`; run against the e2e build; screenshots and results in `docs/verification/`.
# dashboard-ui: requirements

Epic E4 (`docs/bmad/epics-and-sprint.md`). Covers PRD R12, R13, R14, R15, R16, R24 (training UI), N3, N4. Code: `src/` (TypeScript UI, shared later by the Android WebView and the LAN view), `crates/buslink-core/src/alarm/` (alarm engine).
Rules that always apply: `.kiro/steering/ui.md`, `.kiro/steering/safety.md`.

Out of scope: control panel and any write UI (E5), LAN-only build (E7). The UI built here SHALL contain no write, arm or command controls.

## Requirement 1: connection center (R12)

**User story:** As a technician, I want one screen to pick an adapter, set serial or TCP settings, or start Training mode, and see link statistics.

1. THE connection center SHALL list serial ports with name, VID:PID and the chip label from the backend (CH343, CH340, CH9102), and a refresh button.
2. THE user SHALL set baud, data bits, parity and stop bits for RTU, or host and port for Modbus TCP / RTU over TCP, and connect; invalid input SHALL be reported in text next to the field.
3. THE screen SHALL offer "Start Training mode (simulated devices)" that works with no hardware.
4. Each link SHALL show its state (connected, polling, down, disconnected) as text, its kind, a "Simulated" label for simulator links, and per device: requests, GOOD, timeouts, CRC errors, exceptions, decode errors, achieved cycle time and last error.
5. THE screen SHALL show the advice that the CH343G (B) adapter is not isolated and that an isolated adapter and a wired GND are recommended for field work.

## Requirement 2: device library (R9, R10, R12)

1. THE library SHALL list the bundled profiles with vendor, model, version, register count and a support-level badge (text + shape) for `generic`, `documented`, `simulated`, `hardware_verified`.
2. A profile marked `simulated_only` SHALL show "Simulated device" wherever it appears.
3. THE user SHALL add a device to a connected link by choosing a profile, unit ID and poll interval; unit ID 0 SHALL be refused in the form (broadcast) and by the backend.

## Requirement 3: live dashboard (R13, ISA-101)

1. THE dashboard SHALL show L1 overview: one card per device, sorted worst state first (link down/disconnected, then active P1→P3 alarms, then bad quality, then normal), with link state shown separately from value quality.
2. Each tag tile SHALL show tag name, value, unit, a quality text label, data age, and a horizontal analog bar with the normal band and alarm-limit ticks when a range is known.
3. Normal values SHALL be neutral grey; only abnormal states get hue, always with a text label and a non-color cue (hatch, strike-through, outline).
4. A non-GOOD tile SHALL show the last good value dimmed with its age and the quality badge; it SHALL never show 0 or a blank without explanation.
5. A density toggle (comfortable / compact) and a "Pause live updates" control SHALL exist; while paused, a visible "Paused" banner SHALL say that values are not live.

# commissioning-control: requirements

Epic E5 (`docs/bmad/epics-and-sprint.md`). Covers PRD R17, R18, R19 and N1; architecture D8; research/02 §2 (alarms in the report) and §5 (FR2 use control, CR 2.8 auditable events).
Rules that always apply: `.kiro/steering/safety.md` (rules 1–8 in particular), `.kiro/steering/ui.md` (control panel section), `.kiro/steering/modbus.md`.

The command service state machine (`Idle → Armed → Previewed → Confirmed → Sent → ReadBack → Done/Failed`), its audit records and the append-only `command_audit` table already exist (core-protocol Req 16, P10). This epic connects them to the session, the simulator, the Tauri shell and the UI, and adds the commissioning wizard, process feedback, the audit view and the session report.

Out of scope: control of real VFDs or heaters (the control panel exists only for simulated devices), any write through the LAN dashboard or MQTT (E7), user authentication (the role is a local selection and is recorded as such), comm-config registers for the BGT-SMPS soil sensor (its manual in this repo documents none, so its profile declares none).

Decisions recorded with the owner's request (2026-11-13):
- **Arming timeout stays 60 s idle** (safety rule 3 default), not the 120 s in the request. Each preview, confirm or send refreshes it; the countdown shows the time left. `CommandConfig::arm_timeout_ms` makes it configurable for a later decision.
- The stop label is the exact safety-rule text: "Software stop. Not an emergency stop." / "Stop perangkat lunak. Bukan tombol darurat."
- Config registers are declared in the profile's `comm_config` section (schema v1), not in `commands`.

## Requirement 1: arming and session integration (R18, N1)

**User story:** As an operator, I want to arm control for one simulated device for a short time, so that nothing is ever written by accident.

1. THE app SHALL start in Monitoring: WHEN the app starts, a link connects or reconnects, or a profile is loaded, THEN no device SHALL be armed.
2. WHEN the operator arms a device, THE system SHALL require the device's link to be polling, record an `arm` audit row (user, local role, device, profile ID + version, unit ID) and show "Armed: control enabled for N s" with a countdown.
3. WHEN no command activity happens for the arming timeout (default 60 s), THE arm SHALL expire, an `arm_expired` row SHALL be recorded, and any preview or confirmation SHALL be dropped.
4. WHEN the device's link disconnects, reconnects, goes down or changes settings, or the app goes to the background, THE arm SHALL be dropped with a `disarm` row naming the reason; nothing SHALL resume automatically after reconnect.
5. WHILE a device is armed, THE only write path SHALL be the command service through the link worker's queue (one master per bus).

## Requirement 2: control panel for simulated devices (R18)

**User story:** As a trainee, I want to run the simulated VFD and temperature controller through guarded commands, so that I learn the command workflow without risk.

1. THE control panel SHALL exist only for profiles with `simulated_only: true` on a simulator link and SHALL show the banner "Simulated device" on every control view.
2. THE VFD panel SHALL offer run, software stop, frequency setpoint, ramp time and fault reset; THE temperature panel SHALL offer setpoint, heater on, software stop (heater off) and output mode auto/manual. Every command SHALL come from the profile's `commands` list or a `read_write` register.
3. WHEN the operator enters a value, THE system SHALL check it against the profile's `write` bounds (`min`/`max`/`step`/`allowed_values`, `valid_range`) and SHALL reject an out-of-bounds value with a text message next to the field; values SHALL never be clamped.
4. BEFORE sending, THE system SHALL show a confirmation dialog with device, unit ID, register (doc address and PDU offset), function, old value, new value in engineering units, raw register value(s) and the encoded frame in hex; the confirm button SHALL name the action and value (e.g. "Apply setpoint 40.0 °C").
5. WHEN confirmed, THE system SHALL send the frame exactly once, never retry it, then read back and report `verified`, `mismatch` or `unknown`; a timeout SHALL be shown as "effect unknown".
6. THE panel SHALL show three separate fields: command sent, write acknowledged, and process feedback. Process feedback SHALL be judged on the live feedback register named by the command's `feedback` entry, with a tolerance and a timeout, and reported as `pending`, `reached`, `not_reached` or `feedback_unavailable` (feedback quality not GOOD). An acknowledged write SHALL never be shown as "reached".
7. WHILE armed, THE software stop SHALL be visible on the panel and labelled "Software stop. Not an emergency stop." (id: "Stop perangkat lunak. Bukan tombol darurat.").
8. Normal states SHALL stay neutral grey; "running" SHALL never be painted green.

## Requirement 3: commissioning wizard (R17)

**User story:** As a commissioning technician, I want to change a device's unit ID or baud rate with a journal and a recovery hint, so that I never lose the device on the bus.

1. THE wizard SHALL be offered only for devices whose profile declares the setting in `comm_config` and whose capability `comm_config` is not `unsupported`; otherwise it SHALL say why it is not available.
2. WHEN the technician starts the wizard, THE system SHALL require the commissioner role, validate the new value (unit ID 1–247 and not used by another device on the link; baud one of the profile's `codes`), and record a `journal` audit row with the old unit ID and serial settings before anything is armed.
3. THE wizard SHALL then arm the device, preview the frame and require confirmation, and send exactly once.
4. IF the device answers with an exception, THEN the wizard SHALL stop at "failed: settings unchanged".
5. WHEN the write was acknowledged or its effect is unknown, AND the profile says `apply: immediate`, THE wizard SHALL offer "Reconnect at the new settings"; for `after_reboot` it SHALL first ask for a power cycle; for `unknown` it SHALL stop at "needs verification". Reconnecting SHALL drop the arm.
6. AFTER reconnecting, THE wizard SHALL read the setting's register at the new settings and mark the run `pass` (value equals the new setting) or `fail`, with a `verify` audit row.
7. IF verification fails, THEN the wizard SHALL show recovery hints with the old settings and offer "Return the link to the old settings" (no write).
8. Writing a `comm_config` register outside the wizard SHALL be rejected.

## Requirement 4: audit log view (N1, CR 2.8)

1. THE audit view SHALL list every audit row of the session (time local + UTC, event, user/role, device, profile version, function, PDU address, old → requested value, request and response hex, exception, acknowledgement, read-back, note).
2. THE user SHALL filter by device, event and text.
3. THE user SHALL export the audit rows as CSV and XLSX with ISO-8601 UTC times, `.` decimals, numbers as numbers and the formula guard on text cells.
4. THE audit table SHALL stay append-only (update and delete are refused by the database).

## Requirement 5: session report (R19)

1. THE report SHALL contain: session ID, start time, app version, platform; devices with profile ID, version, support level and "Simulated device" where it applies; quality statistics per device (sample counts per quality and link counters); alarm activity (counts per priority and the alarm event list); commands with acknowledgement, read-back and process feedback results; commissioning runs with their journal and verification.
2. THE report SHALL be shown in the app, saved as a self-contained HTML file, and printed to PDF through the WebView print dialog.
3. Every device, profile and user string SHALL be rendered as text (never as markup); THE report SHALL say "simulated" for simulated devices and SHALL make no hardware claim.

## Requirement 6: simulator support (R10, R24)

1. THE simulated VFD and temperature controller SHALL expose a unit-ID register and a baud-code register (simulator design choices, documented in their profiles).
2. WHEN the unit-ID register is written, THE simulated device SHALL answer from its old unit ID and then answer only at the new one; WHEN the baud code is written, it SHALL answer at the old baud and then only at the new baud.
3. A simulated RTU link SHALL carry its baud rate so that a device at another baud stays silent.

## Requirement 7: verification

1. Property tests SHALL show that a frame is never sent unarmed, unconfirmed, after its arm expired, or twice for one confirmation, and that bounds are always enforced.
2. Simulator integration tests SHALL cover the VFD journey (arm, set 30.0 Hz, read-back verified, run, reached target, software stop, audit) and the temperature-controller journey (setpoint, heater on, reached target, software stop), plus the wizard for unit ID and baud.
3. A headless check of PRD journey 4 SHALL drive the e2e build and store screenshots and results in `docs/verification/`.

Process feedback SHALL be judged on the live feedback register named by the command's `feedback` entry, with a tolerance and a timeout, and reported as `pending`, `reached`, `not_reached` or `feedback_unavailable` (feedback quality not GOOD). An acknowledged write SHALL never be shown as "reached".
7. WHILE armed, THE software stop SHALL be visible on the panel and labelled "Software stop. Not an emergency stop." (id: "Stop perangkat lunak. Bukan tombol darurat.").
8. Normal states SHALL stay neutral grey; "running" SHALL never be painted green.

## Requirement 3: commissioning wizard (R17)

**User story:** As a commissioning technician, I want to change a device's unit ID or baud rate with a journal and a recovery hint, so that I never lose the device on the bus.

1. THE wizard SHALL be offered only for devices whose profile declares the setting in `comm_config` and whose capability `comm_config` is not `unsupported`; otherwise it SHALL say why it is not available.
2. WHEN the technician starts the wizard, THE system SHALL require the commissioner role, validate the new value (unit ID 1–247 and not used by another device on the link; baud one of the profile's `codes`), and record a `journal` audit row with the old unit ID and serial settings before anything is armed.
3. THE wizard SHALL then arm the device, preview the frame and require confirmation, and send exactly once.
4. IF the device answers with an exception, THEN the wizard SHALL stop at "failed: settings unchanged".
5. WHEN the write was acknowledged or its effect is unknown, AND the profile says `apply: immediate`, THE wizard SHALL offer "Reconnect at the new settings"; for `after_reboot` it SHALL first ask for a power cycle; for `unknown` it SHALL stop at "needs verification". Reconnecting SHALL drop the arm.
6. AFTER reconnecting, THE wizard SHALL read the setting's register at the new settings and mark the run `pass` (value equals the new setting) or `fail`, with a `verify` audit row.
7. IF verification fails, THEN the wizard SHALL show recovery hints with the old settings and offer "Return the link to the old settings" (no write).
8. Writing a `comm_config` register outside the wizard SHALL be rejected.

1. THE audit view SHALL list every audit row of the session (time local + UTC, event, user/role, device, profile version, function, PDU address, old → requested value, request and response hex, exception, acknowledgement, read-back, note).
2. THE user SHALL filter by device, event and text.
3. THE user SHALL export the audit rows as CSV and XLSX with ISO-8601 UTC times, `.` decimals, numbers as numbers and the formula guard on text cells.
4. THE audit table SHALL stay append-only (update and delete are refused by the database).

## Requirement 5: session report (R19)

1. THE report SHALL contain: session ID, start time, app version, platform; devices with profile ID, version, support level and "Simulated device" where it applies; quality statistics per device (sample counts per quality and link counters); alarm activity (counts per priority and the alarm event list); commands with acknowledgement, read-back and process feedback results; commissioning runs with their journal and verification.
2. THE report SHALL be shown in the app, saved as a self-contained HTML file, and printed to PDF through the WebView print dialog.
3. Every device, profile and user string SHALL be rendered as text (never as markup); THE report SHALL say "simulated" for simulated devices and SHALL make no hardware claim.

## Requirement 6: simulator support (R10, R24)

1. THE simulated VFD and temperature controller SHALL expose a unit-ID register and a baud-code register (simulator design choices, documented in their profiles).
2. WHEN the unit-ID register is written, THE simulated device SHALL answer from its old unit ID and then answer only at the new one; WHEN the baud code is written, it SHALL answer at the old baud and then only at the new baud.
3. A simulated RTU link SHALL carry its baud rate so that a device at another baud stays silent.

## Requirement 7: verification

1. Property tests SHALL show that a frame is never sent unarmed, unconfirmed, after its arm expired, or twice for one confirmation, and that bounds are always enforced.
2. Simulator integration tests SHALL cover the VFD journey (arm, set 30.0 Hz, read-back verified, run, reached target, software stop, audit) and the temperature-controller journey (setpoint, heater on, reached target, software stop), plus the wizard for unit ID and baud.
