# commissioning-control: design

## 1. Module layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `crates/buslink-core/src/command/mod.rs` | Existing state machine (D8). New: `CommandRequest::CommConfig`, `Compare::Deferred` (read-back after reconnect), `journal()`/`note()` audit rows without arming, rejection of comm-config registers outside the wizard. |
| `crates/buslink-core/src/command/feedback.rs` | `FeedbackWatch`: pure judge of "process reached target" from live samples (tolerance, timeout, bit). |
| `crates/buslink-core/src/command/commission.rs` | `Wizard` state for one unit-ID or baud change: journal → armed → previewed → sent → reconnected → pass/fail. |
| `crates/buslink-core/src/command/control.rs` | `Control`: the app-facing façade over `Session` + `CommandService` + wizard + feedback. The Tauri shell holds one. |
| `crates/buslink-core/src/session/mod.rs` | Link generation counter; `command_access` (target + worker handle); `set_device_unit`; `reconfigure_serial`; audit sink to the historian; audit rows; report data. No write is encoded here. |
| `crates/buslink-core/src/export/report.rs` | `ReportData` (devices, quality counts, counters, alarms, commands, commissioning). |
| `crates/buslink-core/src/export/audit.rs` | Audit CSV and XLSX. |
| `crates/buslink-sim/src/devices/comm.rs` | `CommRegs`: unit-ID and baud-code registers shared by the VFD and the temperature controller. |
| `crates/buslink-sim/src/world.rs`, `transport.rs` | Per-device baud; re-keying a device after a unit-ID change; `SimTransport::rtu_at(baud)`. |
| `src-tauri/src/control.rs` | IPC for control, wizard, audit and report. Requests carry IDs and engineering values only, never frames. |
| `src/views/control.ts`, `commission.ts`, `audit.ts`, `report.ts`, `src/components/confirm.ts` | UI. |

## 2. Arming and link generation

`Session` keeps `generation: u64` per link, bumped by connect, reconnect, disconnect, link down and `reconfigure_serial`. `Control::arm` stores `(link_id, generation)`. Every `Control` call first runs `check_link()`: if the generation changed or the link is no longer polling, it calls `CommandService::disarm(Reconnect | Disconnect | LinkLost)` and remembers the reason for the status view. Pull-based checks cannot miss a reconnect that happened between two calls, because the counter only grows.

`command_access(device)` returns a clone of the device, link config and profile plus the worker's `LinkHandle` (timeout = device response timeout). The handle sends jobs to the same worker queue that polls (safety rule 9). The link must be polling.

App background: the webview sends `control_disarm { reason: "app_background" }` on `visibilitychange → hidden`; the shell also disarms on window close.

Arming timeout: `DEFAULT_ARM_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` idle (safety rule 3), refreshed by arm, preview, confirm and execute. The request asked for 120 s; the safety rule wins and the deviation is listed in requirements.md.

## 3. Comm-config requests

`CommandRequest::CommConfig { setting: UnitId | Baud, value: u32 }`:

1. The profile must declare `comm_config.<setting>` and `capabilities.comm_config` ≠ `unsupported`; role must be commissioner.
2. Unit ID: 1–247 (`BroadcastRejected` for 0). Baud: the raw code is looked up in `codes`; a baud with no code is rejected.
3. The raw value then passes the normal register bounds check and encoding.
4. Read-back is `Deferred`: `execute` does not read at the old settings (the device has moved) and reports `readback: unknown` with the note "verified after reconnect at the new settings".
5. `SetRegister`/`Named` on a register named in `comm_config` → `ControlNotAllowed("use the commissioning wizard")`.

Audit events added: `journal` (old settings before arming), `verify` (wizard result), `feedback` (process reached target or not).

## 4. Wizard (`commission.rs` + `Control`)

```
Journaled → (arm) → Armed → (preview) → Previewed → (confirm+execute) → Sent
Sent ─ exception ─────────────────────────────→ Failed("settings unchanged")
Sent ─ ack/unknown, apply=immediate ──────────→ AwaitReconnect
Sent ─ ack/unknown, apply=after_reboot ───────→ AwaitPowerCycle → AwaitReconnect
Sent ─ ack/unknown, apply=unknown ────────────→ NeedsVerification (stop)
AwaitReconnect → (reconnect: set_device_unit | reconfigure_serial; disarm) → Reconnected
Reconnected → (verify: read the setting register at the new settings) → Passed | Failed
Failed/NeedsVerification → (revert: link back to the old settings, no write) → Reverted
```

Each transition is driven by an explicit operator action; nothing advances on a timer and the write is never re-sent. A new write needs a new wizard run. The wizard view carries `old` and `new` settings, so the recovery hint ("The device may still answer at unit 2, 9600 8N1") is always available.

A baud change applies to the whole link: other devices on the same bus stop answering until they are changed too. The wizard says so before arming.

## 5. Process feedback (`feedback.rs`)

Command profile entry, new optional key (schema v1 addition, all three validators):

```json
"feedback": { "register": "output_freq", "tolerance": 0.05, "timeout_ms": 65000, "value": 0, "bit": 0 }
```

- Target = `value` if present, else the commanded engineering value (setpoints).
- `bit` (bitfield registers only) compares that bit with `value` (0 or 1).
- `FeedbackWatch::observe(sample, now)`: quality ≠ GOOD → `feedback_unavailable` while pending (it never counts as reached); GOOD within tolerance → `reached` (latched); deadline passed → `not_reached`. Only samples newer than the command are used.
- `Control::status()` evaluates the watch against the live store and records one `feedback` audit row when it resolves.

Feedback mapping in the simulated profiles (version 1.1.0):

| Profile | Command | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| VFD | run | `status_word` bit 0 = 1, 3 s |
| VFD | stop | `output_freq` = 0 ± 0.05 Hz, 65 s |
| VFD | set_frequency | `output_freq` = setpoint ± 0.05 Hz, 65 s (stays `pending`/`not_reached` while stopped) |
| VFD | reset_fault | `fault_code` = 0, 3 s |
| VFD | set_ramp | none (parameter; read-back only) |
| Temp | set_temperature | `pv` = setpoint ± 1.0 °C, 15 min |
| Temp | heater_off | `output` = 0 ± 0.05 %, 5 s |
| Temp | heater_on, mode_* | none |

## 6. Simulator comm registers

Holding 10 = unit ID (rw 1–247), holding 11 = baud code (rw `0` 4800, `1` 9600, `2` 19200, `3` 38400). Both `apply: immediate`, role commissioner, risk high. The model validates, answers the write at the old settings, and leaves a pending change that the world applies after building the reply: a new unit ID re-keys the device (refused if the ID is taken: the write is acknowledged but the device stays, so verification fails, as a real collision would); a new baud sets the device baud. `SimTransport` in RTU mode carries the link baud; a device with another baud stays silent. MBAP links ignore baud.

## 7. IPC (`src-tauri/src/control.rs`)

`control_status`, `control_arm {device_id, user, role}`, `control_disarm {reason}`, `control_preview {device_id, request}`, `control_confirm {preview_id}`, `control_execute`, `control_cancel`, `wizard_start {device_id, setting, value, user}`, `wizard_preview`, `wizard_execute`, `wizard_power_cycled`, `wizard_reconnect`, `wizard_verify`, `wizard_revert`, `wizard_close`, `audit_list`, `audit_export {format}`, `report_data`, `report_save_html {html}`.
`request` is `{kind: "named", command, value?}` or `{kind: "register", register, value}`. No IPC takes a frame, an address or a function code. `report_save_html` accepts only text up to 5 MB and writes through the save dialog.

## 8. UI

- **Control view** (`#/control/<device>`): banner "Simulated device"; arm form (user name, local role); armed border + "Armed: control enabled for 52 s"; command buttons built from the profile; value fields with bounds hints; software stop button with the safety label, separated from Run by other controls; three result fields (sent / acknowledged / process feedback) plus read-back. Status polled at 2 Hz while the view is open.
- **Confirm dialog** (`components/confirm.ts`): `<dialog>` with focus trap and restore; shows every field of safety rule 3; the confirm button label names the action and value.
- **Wizard view** (`#/commission/<device>`): steps list with the current step marked by text and shape; recovery box always visible after sending.
- **Audit view** (`#/audit`): filterable table; CSV/XLSX export.
- **Report view** (`#/report`): rendered with DOM text nodes; "Save HTML" serializes the report element (text already escaped by the DOM) with inline print styles; "Print / save as PDF" calls `window.print()`; print CSS hides navigation.
- The views render nothing but a notice when there is no backend (LAN/static build).

## 9. Correctness properties

- **C1** (`tests/command_props.rs`, extends P10): random operation sequences including clock jumps past the arm timeout; no frame leaves unless the current preview was confirmed while armed and unexpired; one frame per confirmation.
- **C2**: random values for every writable register of the simulated profiles: the service accepts exactly the values inside the profile bounds, and every sent raw value decodes inside them.
- **C3**: comm-config requests: wrong role, unit 0/248, baud without code, comm register through `SetRegister` → rejected and nothing sent.
- **C4** (`feedback.rs` unit tests): non-GOOD samples never resolve to `reached`; old samples are ignored; deadline gives `not_reached`.
- **J1/J2** (`crates/buslink-sim/tests/control_journeys.rs`, manual clock): VFD and temperature journeys over the simulator.
- **J3** (`crates/buslink-sim/tests/control_session.rs`, real clock): `Control` + `Session` + training bus: journey 4, disarm on reconnect, wizard unit ID and baud pass, wizard failure + revert.

```

Sent ─ exception ─────────────────────────────→ Failed("settings unchanged")
Sent ─ ack/unknown, apply=immediate ──────────→ AwaitReconnect
Sent ─ ack/unknown, apply=after_reboot ───────→ AwaitPowerCycle → AwaitReconnect
Sent ─ ack/unknown, apply=unknown ────────────→ NeedsVerification (stop)
AwaitReconnect → (reconnect: set_device_unit | reconfigure_serial; disarm) → Reconnected
Reconnected → (verify: read the setting register at the new settings) → Passed | Failed
Failed/NeedsVerification → (revert: link back to the old settings, no write) → Reverted
```

Each transition is driven by an explicit operator action; nothing advances on a timer and the write is never re-sent. A new write needs a new wizard run. The wizard view carries `old` and `new` settings, so the recovery hint ("The device may still answer at unit 2, 9600 8N1") is always available.

A baud change applies to the whole link: other devices on the same bus stop answering until they are changed too. The wizard says so before arming.

## 5. Process feedback (`feedback.rs`)

Command profile entry, new optional key (schema v1 addition, all three validators):

```json
"feedback": { "register": "output_freq", "tolerance": 0.05, "timeout_ms": 65000, "value": 0, "bit": 0 }
```

- Target = `value` if present, else the commanded engineering value (setpoints).
- `bit` (bitfield registers only) compares that bit with `value` (0 or 1).

Feedback mapping in the simulated profiles (version 1.1.0):

| Profile | Command | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| VFD | run | `status_word` bit 0 = 1, 3 s |
| VFD | stop | `output_freq` = 0 ± 0.05 Hz, 65 s |
| VFD | set_frequency | `output_freq` = setpoint ± 0.05 Hz, 65 s (stays `pending`/`not_reached` while stopped) |
| VFD | reset_fault | `fault_code` = 0, 3 s |
| VFD | set_ramp | none (parameter; read-back only) |
| Temp | set_temperature | `pv` = setpoint ± 1.0 °C, 15 min |
| Temp | heater_off | `output` = 0 ± 0.05 %, 5 s |
| Temp | heater_on, mode_* | none |

Holding 10 = unit ID (rw 1–247), holding 11 = baud code (rw `0` 4800, `1` 9600, `2` 19200, `3` 38400). Both `apply: immediate`, role commissioner, risk high. The model validates, answers the write at the old settings, and leaves a pending change that the world applies after building the reply: a new unit ID re-keys the device (refused if the ID is taken: the write is acknowledged but the device stays, so verification fails, as a real collision would); a new baud sets the device baud. `SimTransport` in RTU mode carries the link baud; a device with another baud stays silent. MBAP links ignore baud.

## 7. IPC (`src-tauri/src/control.rs`)

`control_status`, `control_arm {device_id, user, role}`, `control_disarm {reason}`, `control_preview {device_id, request}`, `control_confirm {preview_id}`, `control_execute`, `control_cancel`, `wizard_start {device_id, setting, value, user}`, `wizard_preview`, `wizard_execute`, `wizard_power_cycled`, `wizard_reconnect`, `wizard_verify`, `wizard_revert`, `wizard_close`, `audit_list`, `audit_export {format}`, `report_data`, `report_save_html {html}`.
`request` is `{kind: "named", command, value?}` or `{kind: "register", register, value}`. No IPC takes a frame, an address or a function code. `report_save_html` accepts only text up to 5 MB and writes through the save dialog.

## 8. UI

- **Control view** (`#/control/<device>`): banner "Simulated device"; arm form (user name, local role); armed border + "Armed: control enabled for 52 s"; command buttons built from the profile; value fields with bounds hints; software stop button with the safety label, separated from Run by other controls; three result fields (sent / acknowledged / process feedback) plus read-back. Status polled at 2 Hz while the view is open.
- **Confirm dialog** (`components/confirm.ts`): `<dialog>` with focus trap and restore; shows every field of safety rule 3; the confirm button label names the action and value.
- **Wizard view** (`#/commission/<device>`): steps list with the current step marked by text and shape; recovery box always visible after sending.
- **Audit view** (`#/audit`): filterable table; CSV/XLSX export.
- **Report view** (`#/report`): rendered with DOM text nodes; "Save HTML" serializes the report element (text already escaped by the DOM) with inline print styles; "Print / save as PDF" calls `window.print()`; print CSS hides navigation.
- The views render nothing but a notice when there is no backend (LAN/static build).

## 9. Correctness properties

- **C1** (`tests/command_props.rs`, extends P10): random operation sequences including clock jumps past the arm timeout; no frame leaves unless the current preview was confirmed while armed and unexpired; one frame per confirmation.
- **C2**: random values for every writable register of the simulated profiles: the service accepts exactly the values inside the profile bounds, and every sent raw value decodes inside them.
- **C3**: comm-config requests: wrong role, unit 0/248, baud without code, comm register through `SetRegister` → rejected and nothing sent.
- **C4** (`feedback.rs` unit tests): non-GOOD samples never resolve to `reached`; old samples are ignored; deadline gives `not_reached`.
- **J1/J2** (`crates/buslink-sim/tests/control_journeys.rs`, manual clock): VFD and temperature journeys over the simulator.
- **J3** (`crates/buslink-sim/tests/control_session.rs`, real clock): `Control` + `Session` + training bus: journey 4, disarm on reconnect, wizard unit ID and baud pass, wizard failure + revert.

# BusLink device profile schema, version 1

Status: draft written during workspace setup (2026-11-11). The spec session should adopt or amend it; `tools/hooks/check_profile.py` is the executable definition and must change together with this page.

A profile is one JSON file in `profiles/` that describes one device model. It is **data, never code**: keys are strict, unknown keys are errors, and there is no script, expression or template field. The only transform is `engineering = raw × scale + offset`.

Instance settings (which COM port or USB adapter, the unit ID actually used on site, location, names) belong to the project file, not to the profile. One profile serves many devices.

## Top level

| Key | Req. | Type / values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | yes | `1` | |
| `profile_id` | yes | `^[a-z0-9]+([._-][a-z0-9]+)*$`, 3–64 chars | Stable ID, e.g. `bgt.smps-8in1`. |
| `profile_version` | yes | `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` | Any mapping change makes a new version. Every sample and export stores it. |
| `vendor`, `model` | yes | text ≤ 80 | |
| `category`, `firmware` | no | text | `firmware` = range the mapping applies to. |
| `description`, `notes` | no | text, or `{ "en", "id" }` | |
| `support_level` | yes | `generic` · `documented` · `simulated` · `hardware_verified` | Overall label shown in the UI. |
| `capabilities` | no | `{ read, write, comm_config, control }`, each a level or `unsupported` | Read support does not imply write or control support. |
| `simulated_only` | no | bool | `true` for devices that exist only in the simulator (VFD, temperature controller). |
| `source` | if documented / hardware_verified | `{ document, revision, url?, pages?, retrieved?, publisher? }` | The manual the mapping came from. |
| `evidence` | if hardware_verified | `{ hardware: [ { date, adapter, platform, record, result, unit_id?, firmware?, notes? } ] }` | At least one `result: "pass"` with a `record` (path or URL of the log or video). |
| `transport` | yes | `{ rtu?, tcp?, simulator? }` | Defaults only; never assume they are universal. |
| `registers` | yes | list, 1–2000 | See below. |
| `commands` | no | list | Control actions. **Only on `simulated_only` profiles in v1.** |
| `comm_config` | no | `{ unit_id?, baud? }` | For the commissioning wizard. |

### Support levels

- `generic`: mapping typed in by a user; no identification claim.
- `documented`: derived from a named manual revision and checked statically.
- `simulated`: codec and operations pass against the built-in simulator. This is not evidence for hardware.
- `hardware_verified`: a specific model + firmware + adapter + platform combination has a recorded passing test. A `simulated_only` profile can never reach this level.

## `transport`

- `rtu`: `unit_id` 1–247 (0 is broadcast and is never a default), `baud` 300–3 000 000 (warning if non-standard), `data_bits` 7|8, `parity` `none`|`even`|`odd`, `stop_bits` 1|2, optional `response_timeout_ms` 50–10 000 and `inter_frame_ms` 0–1000.
- `tcp`: `unit_id` 1–255, `port` 1–65535, optional `response_timeout_ms`.
- `simulator`: `{ "model": "<simulator id>" }`.

## Register entries

| Key | Req. | Values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$`, unique | |
| `name` | yes | text ≤ 80 or `{ "en", "id" }` | Both languages required when bilingual. |
| `table` | yes | `coil` · `discrete_input` · `input_register` · `holding_register` | |
| `address` | yes | integer 0–65535 | **Zero-based PDU offset.** Never the 4xxxx label. |
| `doc_address` | no | string or int | The label exactly as printed in the manual (e.g. `"40001"`). |
| `type` | yes | `bool` · `u16` · `i16` · `bitfield` · `u32` · `i32` · `f32` · `u64` · `i64` · `f64` · `string` | `bool` only in coil/discrete tables, never in register tables. |
| `length` | string only | registers, 1–125 | |
| `word_order` | 32/64-bit: yes | `ABCD` · `CDAB` · `BADC` · `DCBA` | Strings may use `ABCD` or `BADC`. Not allowed on 16-bit types. See `.kiro/steering/modbus.md`. |
| `scale`, `offset` | no | number (scale ≠ 0) | Defaults 1 and 0. |
| `unit`, `decimals` | no | text ≤ 16, int 0–9 | |
| `valid_range` | no | `[min, max]` in engineering units | Out of range → `DECODE_ERROR`. |
| `invalid_sentinels` | no | list of raw ints | E.g. `32767` for "sensor open". |
| `bits` | bitfield only | `{ "0".."15": label }` | |
| `poll` | no | `fast` · `normal` · `slow` | Scheduling hint. |
| `source_page` | no | text ≤ 40 | Page or table in `source.document`. |
| `access` | no | `read` (default) · `read_write` | `read_write` only in `coil` and `holding_register`. |
| `write` | if read_write | `{ min, max, step?, allowed_values?, risk, role, confirm?, readback? }` | `risk`: `low`/`medium`/`high`; `role`: `operator`/`commissioner`. Numeric writes need `min`+`max` (inside `valid_range`) or `allowed_values`. `confirm` and `readback` may only be `true`. |

Registers that overlap in the same table produce a warning (aliases are allowed but must be deliberate).

## `commands` (simulated devices only in v1)

`{ id, kind, label, register, readback_register, value?, expected?, timeout_ms? }`

- `kind`: `run` · `stop` · `setpoint` · `reset_fault` · `mode`.
- `register` must be a `read_write` register of the same profile; `readback_register` is required.
- `setpoint` has no fixed `value`: the operator enters it and the register's `write` bounds apply. Other kinds need a numeric `value`.
- The command service still applies arming, confirmation, read-back and audit (`.kiro/steering/safety.md`).

## `comm_config`

`{ "unit_id": { register, apply }, "baud": { register, apply, codes: { "<raw>": <baud> } } }` with `apply` = `immediate` · `after_reboot` · `unknown`. The register must be `read_write`. If `apply` is `unknown`, the wizard stops at "needs verification" instead of retrying.

## Validation

```sh
python3 tools/hooks/check_profile.py profiles/<file>.json        # one file
find profiles -name '*.json' -exec python3 tools/hooks/check_profile.py {} +
```

The `profile-schema-check` hook runs the same check when a file under `profiles/` is saved.

Three validators implement this page and must stay in step:

- `profiles/schema/buslink-profile.schema.json` (JSON Schema 2020-12) covers structure, enums and ranges, for editors. Files under `profiles/schema/` are not profiles and the hook skips them.
- `tools/hooks/check_profile.py` (hook, stdlib only). `--json` prints one JSON verdict per file.
- `crates/buslink-core/src/profile/validate.rs`, used by the app when loading a profile. `crates/buslink-core/tests/profile_agreement.rs` checks that it gives the same verdict and the same error and warning paths as the Python script, on the bundled profiles, the fixtures in `crates/buslink-core/tests/fixtures/profiles/` and several hundred mutated documents.

Strictness rules added with the Rust validator (2026-11-12), applied by both:

- `null` is never a value: omit the key instead.
- Enum values are type-strict: `8.0` is not `8` and `true` is not `1`.
- IDs, versions, dates, bit indexes and baud codes are matched over the whole string, ASCII only (so `"1.0.0\n"` and non-ASCII digits are rejected).
- `NaN` and `Infinity` are not JSON; integers must fit in 64 bits.
- `$schema` and `$comment` must be strings; command `expected` must be a number; `source.publisher` and evidence `firmware` and `notes` are checked as text.

- `rtu`: `unit_id` 1–247 (0 is broadcast and is never a default), `baud` 300–3 000 000 (warning if non-standard), `data_bits` 7|8, `parity` `none`|`even`|`odd`, `stop_bits` 1|2, optional `response_timeout_ms` 50–10 000 and `inter_frame_ms` 0–1000.
- `tcp`: `unit_id` 1–255, `port` 1–65535, optional `response_timeout_ms`.
- `simulator`: `{ "model": "<simulator id>" }`.

## Register entries

| Key | Req. | Values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$`, unique | |
| `name` | yes | text ≤ 80 or `{ "en", "id" }` | Both languages required when bilingual. |
| `table` | yes | `coil` · `discrete_input` · `input_register` · `holding_register` | |
| `address` | yes | integer 0–65535 | **Zero-based PDU offset.** Never the 4xxxx label. |
| `doc_address` | no | string or int | The label exactly as printed in the manual (e.g. `"40001"`). |
| `type` | yes | `bool` · `u16` · `i16` · `bitfield` · `u32` · `i32` · `f32` · `u64` · `i64` · `f64` · `string` | `bool` only in coil/discrete tables, never in register tables. |
| `length` | string only | registers, 1–125 | |
| `word_order` | 32/64-bit: yes | `ABCD` · `CDAB` · `BADC` · `DCBA` | Strings may use `ABCD` or `BADC`. Not allowed on 16-bit types. See `.kiro/steering/modbus.md`. |
| `scale`, `offset` | no | number (scale ≠ 0) | Defaults 1 and 0. |
| `unit`, `decimals` | no | text ≤ 16, int 0–9 | |
| `valid_range` | no | `[min, max]` in engineering units | Out of range → `DECODE_ERROR`. |
| `invalid_sentinels` | no | list of raw ints | E.g. `32767` for "sensor open". |
| `bits` | bitfield only | `{ "0".."15": label }` | |
| `poll` | no | `fast` · `normal` · `slow` | Scheduling hint. |
| `source_page` | no | text ≤ 40 | Page or table in `source.document`. |
| `access` | no | `read` (default) · `read_write` | `read_write` only in `coil` and `holding_register`. |
| `write` | if read_write | `{ min, max, step?, allowed_values?, risk, role, confirm?, readback? }` | `risk`: `low`/`medium`/`high`; `role`: `operator`/`commissioner`. Numeric writes need `min`+`max` (inside `valid_range`) or `allowed_values`. `confirm` and `readback` may only be `true`. |

Registers that overlap in the same table produce a warning (aliases are allowed but must be deliberate).

## `commands` (simulated devices only in v1)

`{ id, kind, label, register, readback_register, value?, expected?, timeout_ms?, feedback? }`

- `kind`: `run` · `stop` · `setpoint` · `reset_fault` · `mode`.
- `register` must be a `read_write` register of the same profile; `readback_register` is required.
- `setpoint` has no fixed `value`: the operator enters it and the register's `write` bounds apply. Other kinds need a numeric `value`.
- `feedback` (added 2026-11-13, commissioning-control): `{ register, tolerance, timeout_ms, value?, bit? }`. The live register that shows whether the **process** reached the target, which is a different question from the read-back of the written register. `register` is any register of the profile; `tolerance` ≥ 0 in engineering units; `timeout_ms` 100–3 600 000. `value` is the target; it may be omitted only for `setpoint` commands (target = the entered value). `bit` 0–15 compares one bit of a bitfield register with `value` 0 or 1.
- The command service still applies arming, confirmation, read-back and audit (`.kiro/steering/safety.md`).

## `comm_config`

`{ "unit_id": { register, apply }, "baud": { register, apply, codes: { "<raw>": <baud> } } }` with `apply` = `immediate` · `after_reboot` · `unknown`. The register must be `read_write`. If `apply` is `unknown`, the wizard stops at "needs verification" instead of retrying.

## Validation

```sh
python3 tools/hooks/check_profile.py profiles/<file>.json        # one file
find profiles -name '*.json' -exec python3 tools/hooks/check_profile.py {} +
```

The `profile-schema-check` hook runs the same check when a file under `profiles/` is saved.

Three validators implement this page and must stay in step:

- `profiles/schema/buslink-profile.schema.json` (JSON Schema 2020-12) covers structure, enums and ranges, for editors. Files under `profiles/schema/` are not profiles and the hook skips them.
- `tools/hooks/check_profile.py` (hook, stdlib only). `--json` prints one JSON verdict per file.
- `crates/buslink-core/src/profile/validate.rs`, used by the app when loading a profile. `crates/buslink-core/tests/profile_agreement.rs` checks that it gives the same verdict and the same error and warning paths as the Python script, on the bundled profiles, the fixtures in `crates/buslink-core/tests/fixtures/profiles/` and several hundred mutated documents.

Strictness rules added with the Rust validator (2026-11-12), applied by both:

- `null` is never a value: omit the key instead.
- Enum values are type-strict: `8.0` is not `8` and `true` is not `1`.
- IDs, versions, dates, bit indexes and baud codes are matched over the whole string, ASCII only (so `"1.0.0\n"` and non-ASCII digits are rejected).
- `NaN` and `Infinity` are not JSON; integers must fit in 64 bits.
- `$schema` and `$comment` must be strings; command `expected` must be a number; `source.publisher` and evidence `firmware` and `notes` are checked as text.

//! XLSX export: sheets Measurements, Devices, Configuration, Events, Commands.
//! Numbers are written as numbers; text cells pass through the formula guard
//! and are written as strings (never as formulas).

use super::{ExportDoc, MEASUREMENT_COLUMNS, guard_text, raw_hex};
use crate::time::iso8601_utc_ms;
use rust_xlsxwriter::{Workbook, Worksheet, XlsxError};

enum Cell {
    Text(String),
    Num(Option<f64>),
}

fn t(s: &str) -> Cell {
    Cell::Text(s.to_owned())
}
fn ot(s: Option<&str>) -> Cell {
    Cell::Text(s.unwrap_or_default().to_owned())
}
fn n<T: Into<f64>>(v: Option<T>) -> Cell {
    Cell::Num(v.map(Into::into))
}

fn write_rows(ws: &mut Worksheet, header: &[&str], rows: Vec<Vec<Cell>>) -> Result<(), XlsxError> {
    for (c, h) in header.iter().enumerate() {
        ws.write_string(0, c as u16, *h)?;
    }
    for (r, cells) in rows.into_iter().enumerate() {
        let r = (r + 1) as u32;
        for (c, cell) in cells.into_iter().enumerate() {
            let c = c as u16;
            match cell {
                Cell::Text(s) if !s.is_empty() => {
                    ws.write_string(r, c, guard_text(&s))?;
                }
                Cell::Num(Some(v)) if v.is_finite() => {
                    ws.write_number(r, c, v)?;
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
    ws.set_freeze_panes(1, 0)?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Integers above 2^53 are not exact as XLSX numbers, so they go out as text.
fn int_cell(v: u64) -> Cell {
    if v <= (1u64 << 53) {
        Cell::Num(Some(v as f64))
    } else {
        Cell::Text(v.to_string())
    }
}

pub fn workbook(doc: &ExportDoc) -> Result<Vec<u8>, XlsxError> {
    let mut wb = Workbook::new();

    let ws = wb.add_worksheet();
    ws.set_name("Measurements")?;

fn happy_path_preview_confirm_execute_readback_audit() {
    let mut w = World::new();
    let audit = MemoryAudit::new();
    let mut svc = service(&w, &audit);
    svc.arm(target("sim-vfd.json", &sim_link("sim"), 2), op(Role::Operator))
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(svc.state(), CommandState::Armed);
    let p = svc.preview(&mut w.link(), set("freq_setpoint", 30.0)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        (p.unit_id, p.address, p.function, p.old_value, p.new_value),
        (2, 1, 0x06, Some(0.0), 30.0)
    );
    assert_eq!(p.raw_registers, vec![3000]);
    assert_eq!(p.pdu_hex, "06 00 01 0B B8");
    let expected_frame = rtu::encode_adu(2, &[0x06, 0x00, 0x01, 0x0B, 0xB8]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.frame_hex, buslink_core::testkit::hex(&expected_frame));
    assert!(p.simulated);
    assert!(w.write_frames().is_empty(), "preview never writes");
    svc.confirm(p.id).unwrap();
    assert!(w.write_frames().is_empty(), "confirm never writes");
    let o = svc.execute(&mut w.link()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        (o.ack.clone(), o.readback, o.readback_value),
        (Ack::Acknowledged, Readback::Verified, Some(30.0))
    );
    assert_eq!(svc.state(), CommandState::Done);
    assert_eq!(w.write_frames(), vec![expected_frame]);
    assert_eq!(w.bus.with(2, |u| u.holding[&1]), 3000);
    let events: Vec<AuditEvent> = audit.records().iter().map(|r| r.event.unwrap()).collect();
    assert_eq!(
        events,
        vec![
            AuditEvent::Arm,
            AuditEvent::Preview,
            AuditEvent::Confirm,
            AuditEvent::Sent,
            AuditEvent::Result
        ]
    );
    let last = audit.records().last().unwrap().clone();
    assert_eq!(last.session_id, "session-1");
    assert_eq!((last.user.as_str(), last.role.as_str()), ("tech1", "operator"));
    assert_eq!(
        (last.profile_id.as_str(), last.profile_version.as_str()),
        ("sim.vfd-basic", "1.1.0")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        (last.function, last.address, last.old_value, last.requested_value),
        (Some(6), Some(1), Some(0.0), Some(30.0))
    );
    assert!(last.request_hex.is_some() && last.response_hex.as_deref().is_some_and(|s| !s.is_empty()));
    assert_eq!(last.readback.as_deref(), Some("verified"));
}

#[test]
fn bounds_are_rejected_never_clamped() {
    let mut w = World::new();
    let audit = MemoryAudit::new();
    let mut svc = service(&w, &audit);
    svc.arm(target("sim-vfd.json", &sim_link("sim"), 2), op(Role::Operator))
        .unwrap();
    for (reg, v) in [
        ("freq_setpoint", 50.01),
        ("freq_setpoint", -0.01),
        ("freq_setpoint", 30.005),
        ("control_word", 2.0),
        ("freq_setpoint", f64::NAN),
    ] {
        let e = svc.preview(&mut w.link(), set(reg, v)).unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(e, CommandError::OutOfBounds(_)), "{reg}={v}: {e:?}");
    }
    assert!(matches!(
        svc.preview(&mut w.link(), set("output_freq", 1.0)),
        Err(CommandError::NotWritable(_))
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        svc.preview(&mut w.link(), set("nope", 1.0)),
        Err(CommandError::UnknownRegister(_))
    ));
    assert!(w.write_frames().is_empty());
    assert!(audit.records().iter().any(|r| r.event == Some(AuditEvent::Rejected)));
    // A valid value still works afterwards.
    svc.preview(&mut w.link(), set("freq_setpoint", 50.0)).unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn role_and_arming_rules() {
    let mut w = World::new();
    let audit = MemoryAudit::new();
    let mut svc = service(&w, &audit);
    let t = target("sim-vfd.json", &sim_link("sim"), 2);
    assert!(matches!(
        svc.arm(t.clone(), op(Role::Viewer)),
        Err(CommandError::Role { .. })
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        svc.preview(&mut w.link(), set("freq_setpoint", 1.0)),
        Err(CommandError::NotArmed)
    ));
    svc.arm(t.clone(), op(Role::Operator)).unwrap();
    // ramp_time needs the commissioner role.
    assert!(matches!(
        svc.preview(&mut w.link(), set("ramp_time", 10.0)),
        Err(CommandError::Role {
            need: "commissioner",
            ..
        })
    ));
    svc.arm(t.clone(), op(Role::Commissioner)).unwrap();
    svc.preview(&mut w.link(), set("ramp_time", 10.0)).unwrap();
    // Expiry after 60 s idle, measured from the last action.
    w.clock.advance(59_000);
    let p = svc.preview(&mut w.link(), set("ramp_time", 12.0)).unwrap();
    w.clock.advance(59_000);
    svc.confirm(p.id).unwrap();

    ] {

/* ---------- alarms ---------- */

  display: grid;

}
.exercises {
  padding-left: 0;
  list-style: none;
}

/* ---------- narrow screens (Android, 360 px) ---------- */

  *,
  *::before,
  *::after {
    animation: none !important;
    transition: none !important;
    scroll-behavior: auto !important;
  }
}

<content>
    const grid = h("div", { class: "tile-grid" });
    const tiles = new Map<string, Tile>();
    for (const reg of profile.registers) {
      const tile = new Tile(reg, device.id);
      tiles.set(reg.id, tile);
      grid.append(tile.el);
    }
    const el = h(
      "section",
      { class: "card device-card", "data-device": device.id, "aria-label": device.name },
      head,
      link.simulated || profile.simulated_only ? simulatedBanner() : null,
      grid,
    );

    results.trend_render_note = renderNote;
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(OUT, "03-trend-timeout-gap.png"), fullPage: true });

    // Let the fault end so the gap closes and GOOD data resumes.
    await sleep(17000);
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(OUT, "04-trend-after-recovery.png"), fullPage: true });

    await page.evaluate((dev) => (location.hash = `#/inspector/${encodeURIComponent(dev)}`), temp);
    const frames = await waitFor(page, () => document.querySelectorAll(".frames-table tbody tr").length > 0, 10000);
    const frameTimeout = await page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll(".frames-table tbody tr")].some((r) => r.textContent.includes("TIMEOUT")));
    step("register inspector lists frames including the timeouts", frames && frameTimeout);
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(OUT, "05-inspector.png"), fullPage: true });

    await page.evaluate(() => (location.hash = "#/alarms"));
    await page.waitForSelector(".alarm-table, .alarms", { timeout: 10000 });
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(OUT, "06-alarms.png"), fullPage: true });

    await page.evaluate(() => (location.hash = "#/dashboard"));
    await page.waitForSelector("[data-testid=export-csv]", { timeout: 10000 });
    await page.click("[data-testid=export-csv]");
    const saved = await waitFor(page, () => /Saved to|Tersimpan di/.test(document.querySelector(".export-bar .status-line")?.textContent ?? ""), 20000);
    const files = readdirSync(EXPORT_DIR).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".csv"));
    let csvOk = false;
    let csvDetail = "no CSV written";
    if (files[0]) {
      const lines = readFileSync(join(EXPORT_DIR, files[0]), "utf8").split(/\r?\n/);
      const header = lines[0] ?? "";
      const timeouts = lines.filter((l) => l.includes(temp) && l.includes("TIMEOUT")).length;
      const goods = lines.filter((l) => l.includes(",GOOD,")).length;
      csvOk = saved && header.includes("quality") && header.includes("age_ms") && timeouts > 0 && goods > 0;
      csvDetail = `${files[0]}: ${lines.length - 1} rows, ${timeouts} TIMEOUT rows for ${temp}, ${goods} GOOD rows; header: ${header}`;
    }
    step("export CSV with quality + age columns and TIMEOUT rows", csvOk, csvDetail);

    // Narrow layout inside the real app (Android-size viewport).
    await page.setViewport({ width: 360, height: 780 });
    await sleep(800);
    const overflow = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth);
    step("app at 360 px: no horizontal page scroll", overflow <= 0, `overflow ${overflow}px`);
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(OUT, "07-dashboard-360px.png"), fullPage: true });
    await page.emulateMediaFeatures([{ name: "prefers-color-scheme", value: "dark" }]);
    await page.evaluate(() => {
      localStorage.setItem("buslink.theme", "system");
      document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "dark";
    });
    await sleep(500);
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(OUT, "08-dashboard-360px-dark.png"), fullPage: true });
    await page.evaluate(() => (document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "light"));
  } catch (e) {
    step("journey ran without an exception", false, String(e?.stack ?? e));
  } finally {
    await browser?.disconnect().catch(() => {});
    app.kill();
  }
}

async function partB() {
  const dist = join(ROOT, "dist");
  if (!existsSync(join(dist, "index.html"))) return step("dist/ built", false);
  const types = { ".html": "text/html", ".js": "text/javascript", ".css": "text/css", ".png": "image/png" };
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    const path = join(dist, (req.url ?? "/").split("?")[0] === "/" ? "index.html" : decodeURIComponent((req.url ?? "").split("?")[0]));
    if (!path.startsWith(dist) || !existsSync(path)) {
      res.writeHead(404).end();
      return;
    }
    res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": types[extname(path)] ?? "application/octet-stream" }).end(readFileSync(path));
  });
  await new Promise((r) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", r));
  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}/`;
  const browser = await puppeteer.launch({ executablePath: CHROME, headless: true, args: ["--no-first-run"] });
  try {
    const page = await browser.newPage();
    for (const [lang, w] of [["en", 360], ["id", 360], ["en", 1280]]) {
      await page.setViewport({ width: w, height: 800 });
      await page.goto(`${url}#/connect`, { waitUntil: "networkidle0" });
      await page.evaluate((l) => localStorage.setItem("buslink.lang", l), lang);
      await page.reload({ waitUntil: "networkidle0" });
      const info = await page.evaluate(() => ({
        overflow: document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth,
        lang: document.documentElement.lang,
        notice: document.querySelector(".notice[role=alert]")?.textContent ?? "",
        smallTargets: [...document.querySelectorAll("button, select, input, .nav a")]
          .filter((e) => e.offsetParent !== null)
          .map((e) => e.getBoundingClientRect())
          .filter((r) => r.height < 24 || r.width < 24).length,
      }));
      step(
        `dist/ in headless Chrome (${lang}, ${w}px): no backend notice, no page overflow, targets ≥ 24 px`,
        info.overflow <= 0 && info.lang === lang && info.notice.length > 0 && info.smallTargets === 0,
        JSON.stringify(info),
      );
</content>
</file>
